How People Use ChatGPT
人们如何使用 ChatGPT
Aaron Chatterji, Thomas Cunningham, David J. Deming, Zoe Hitzig, Christopher Ong, Carl
Aaron Chatterji、Thomas Cunningham、David J. Deming、Zoe Hitzig、Christopher Ong、Carl
Yan Shan, and Kevin Wadman
Yan Shan 和 Kevin Wadman

September 2025
2025 年 9 月

Abstract
摘要

Despite the rapid adoption of LLM chatbots, little is known about how they are used. We document the growth of ChatGPT’s consumer product from its launch in November 2022 through July 2025, when it had been adopted by around 10 % 10 % 10%10 \% of the world’s adult population. Early adopters were disproportionately male but the gender gap has narrowed dramatically, and we find higher growth rates in lower-income countries. Using a privacy-preserving automated pipeline, we classify usage patterns within a representative sample of ChatGPT conversations. We find steady growth in work-related messages but even faster growth in non-work-related messages, which have grown from 53 % 53 % 53%53 \% to more than 70 % 70 % 70%70 \% of all usage. Work usage is more common for educated users in highly-paid professional occupations. We classify messages by conversation topic and find that “Practical Guidance,” “Seeking Information,” and “Writing” are the three most common topics and collectively account for nearly 80 % 80 % 80%80 \% of all conversations. Writing dominates work-related tasks, highlighting chatbots’ unique ability to generate digital outputs compared to traditional search engines. Computer programming and self-expression both represent relatively small shares of use. Overall, we find that ChatGPT provides economic value through decision support, which is especially important in knowledge-intensive jobs.
尽管 LLM 聊天机器人被迅速采用，但人们对其如何被使用知之甚少。我们记录了 ChatGPT 消费产品从 2022 年 11 月发布至 2025 年 7 月的发展情况，到那时其已被全球约 10 % 10 % 10%10 \% 成年人口采用。早期使用者男性占比过高，但性别差距已显著缩小，我们还发现低收入国家的增长率更高。我们使用一种隐私保护的自动化管道，在具有代表性的 ChatGPT 对话样本中对使用模式进行分类。我们发现与工作相关的信息量稳步增长，但非工作相关信息的增长更快，其在所有使用中已从 53 % 53 % 53%53 \% 增长到超过 70 % 70 % 70%70 \% 。受过教育且从事高薪专业职业的用户更常用于工作场景。我们按对话主题对消息进行分类，发现“实用指导”、“寻求信息”和“写作”是三大最常见主题，合计占近 80 % 80 % 80%80 \% 的所有对话。写作在与工作相关的任务中占主导地位，凸显出与传统搜索引擎相比，聊天机器人在生成数字产出方面的独特能力。 计算机编程和自我表达在使用中所占比例均相对较小。总体而言，我们发现 ChatGPT 通过决策支持提供经济价值，这在知识密集型工作中尤为重要。

1 Introduction
1 介绍

ChatGPT launched in November 2022. By July 2025, 18 billion messages were being sent each week by 700 million users, representing around 10 % 10 % 10%10 \% of the global adult population. 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} For a new technology, this speed of global diffusion has no precedent (Bick et al., 2024).
ChatGPT 于 2022 年 11 月推出。截至 2025 年 7 月，每周有 700 百万用户发送 180 亿条消息，约占全球成年人口的 10 % 10 % 10%10 \% 。 1 1 ^(1){ }^{1} 对于一项新技术而言，这种全球传播速度史无前例（Bick et al., 2024）。
This paper studies consumer usage of ChatGPT, the first mass-market chatbot and likely the largest. 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} ChatGPT is based on a Large Language Model (LLM), a type of Artificial Intelligence (AI) developed over the last decade and generally considered to represent an acceleration in AI capabilities. 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
本文研究消费者对 ChatGPT 的使用情况，ChatGPT 是首个大众市场聊天机器人并可能是最大的产品。 2 2 ^(2){ }^{2} ChatGPT 基于 LLM，这是一种在过去十年中发展起来的人工智能（AI）类型，通常被认为代表了 AI 能力的一次加速。 3 3 ^(3){ }^{3}
The sudden growth in LLM abilities and adoption has intensified interest in the effects of artificial intelligence on economic growth (Acemoglu, 2024; Korinek and Suh, 2024); employment (Eloundou et al., 2025); and society (Kulveit et al., 2025). However, despite the rapid adoption of LLMs, there is limited public information on how they are used. A number of surveys have measured self-reported adoption of LLMs (Bick et al., 2024; Pew Research Center, 2025); however there are reasons to expect bias in self-reports (Ling and Imas, 2025), and none of these papers have been able to directly track the quantity or nature of chatbot conversations.
LLM 能力和采用的突然增长加剧了人们对人工智能对经济增长（Acemoglu, 2024；Korinek 和 Suh, 2024）、就业（Eloundou 等人, 2025）和社会（Kulveit 等人, 2025）影响的关注。然而，尽管 LLMs 被迅速采用，但关于其使用方式的公开信息仍然有限。若干调查衡量了自报的 LLMs 采用情况（Bick 等人, 2024；Pew Research Center, 2025）；但有理由预计自报会存在偏差（Ling 和 Imas, 2025），并且这些论文中没有一篇能够直接跟踪聊天机器人对话的数量或性质。
Two recent papers do report statistics on chatbot conversations, classified in a variety of ways (Handa et al., 2025; Tomlinson et al., 2025). We build on this work in several respects. First, the pool of users on ChatGPT is far larger, meaning we expect our data to be a closer approximation to the average chatbot user. 4 4 ^(4){ }^{4} Second, we use automated classifiers to report on the types of messages that users send using new classification taxonomies relative to the existing literature. Third, we report the diffusion of chatbot use across populations and the growth of different types of usage within cohorts. Fourth, we use a secure data clean room protocol to analyze aggregated employment and education categories for a sample of our users, lending new insights about differences in the types of messages sent by different groups while protecting user privacy.
最近有两篇论文报告了关于聊天机器人对话的统计数据，并按多种方式进行了分类（Handa et al., 2025；Tomlinson et al., 2025）。我们在多方面扩展了这项工作。首先，ChatGPT 的用户群体要大得多，这意味着我们预计我们的数据更接近平均聊天机器人用户的情况。其次，我们使用自动分类器来报告用户发送消息的类型，采用了相对于现有文献的新分类法。第三，我们报告了聊天机器人使用在不同人群中的传播情况以及各队列内不同类型使用的增长情况。第四，我们使用安全数据清理室协议来分析样本用户的汇总就业和教育类别，在保护用户隐私的同时为不同群体发送消息类型的差异提供了新的见解。
Our primary sample is a random selection of messages sent to ChatGPT on consumer plans (Free, Plus, Pro) between May 2024 and June 2025. 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} Messages from the user to chatbot are classified automatically using a number of different taxonomies: whether the message is used for paid work, the topic of conversation, and the type of interaction (asking, doing, or expressing), and the O*NET task the user is performing. Each taxonomy is defined in a prompt passed to an LLM, allowing us to classify messages without any human seeing them. We give the text of most prompts in Appendix A along with details about how the prompts were validated in Appendix B. 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} The classification pipeline is protected by a series of privacy measures, detailed below, to ensure no leakage of sensitive information during the automated analysis. In a secure data clean room, we relate taxonomies of messages to aggregated employment and education categories.
我们的主要样本是对 2024 年 5 月至 2025 年 6 月期间发送到 ChatGPT 的消费者计划（Free、Plus、Pro）消息的随机抽样。 5 5 ^(5){ }^{5} 来自用户发送给聊天机器人的消息通过多种不同的分类法自动进行分类：消息是否用于有偿工作、对话主题、交互类型（询问、执行或表达）以及用户正在执行的 O*NET 任务。每个分类法都在传递给 LLM 的提示中定义，使我们能够在没有任何人查看消息的情况下对其进行分类。我们在附录 A 中给出了大多数提示的文本，并在附录 B 中提供了这些提示如何验证的详细信息。 6 6 ^(6){ }^{6} 分类管道受一系列隐私措施保护（详见下文），以确保在自动化分析过程中不会泄露敏感信息。在安全的数据清洁室中，我们将消息的分类法与汇总的就业和教育类别关联起来。

messages have grown continuously, but non-work messages have grown faster and now represent more than 70 % 70 % 70%70 \% of all consumer ChatGPT messages. While most economic analysis of AI has focused on its impact on productivity in paid work, the impact on activity outside of work (home production) is on a similar scale and possibly larger. The decrease in the share of work-related messages is primarily due to changing usage within each cohort of users rather than a change in the composition of new ChatGPT users. This finding is consistent with Collis and Brynjolfsson (2025), who use choice experiments to uncover willingness-to-pay for generative AI and estimate a consumer surplus of at least $ 97 $ 97 $97\$ 97 billion in 2024 alone in the US.
消息量持续增长，但非工作相关消息增长更快，目前已占所有消费者 ChatGPT 消息的超过 70 % 70 % 70%70 \% 。尽管大多数关于 AI 的经济分析集中于其对有偿工作生产率的影响，但对工作之外活动（家庭生产）的影响在规模上相当且可能更大。工作相关消息份额的下降主要是由于每一用户群体内部使用方式的变化，而非新 ChatGPT 用户构成的变化。该结论与 Collis 和 Brynjolfsson（2025）一致，他们通过选择实验揭示了对生成式 AI 的支付意愿，并估计仅在 2024 年美国的消费者剩余至少为 $ 97 $ 97 $97\$ 97 十亿美元。
We next report on a classification of messages using a taxonomy developed at OpenAI for understanding product usage (“conversation classifier”). Nearly 80 % 80 % 80%80 \% of all ChatGPT usage falls into three broad categories, which we call Practical Guidance, Seeking Information, and Writing. Practical Guidance is the most common use case and includes activities like tutoring and teaching, how-to advice about a variety of topics, and creative ideation. 7 7 ^(7){ }^{7} Seeking Information includes searching for information about people, current events, products, and recipes, and appears to be a very close substitute for web search. Writing includes the automated production of emails, documents and other communications, but also editing, critiquing, summarizing, and translating text provided by the user. Writing is the most common use case at work, accounting for 40 % 40 % 40%40 \% of work-related messages on average in June 2025. About two-thirds of all Writing messages ask ChatGPT to modify user text (editing, critiquing, translating, etc.) rather than creating new text from scratch. About 10 % 10 % 10%10 \% of all messages are requests for tutoring or teaching, suggesting that education is a key use case for ChatGPT.
接下来我们报告使用 OpenAI 为理解产品使用而开发的分类法（“对话分类器”）对消息进行分类的结果。几乎 80 % 80 % 80%80 \% 的所有 ChatGPT 使用属于三大类，我们称之为“实用指导”、“寻求信息”和“写作”。“实用指导”是最常见的使用场景，包括辅导与教学、各类主题的操作建议以及创意构思等活动。 7 7 ^(7){ }^{7} “寻求信息”包括搜索关于人物、时事、产品和食谱的信息，并且似乎是网页搜索的非常接近的替代品。“写作”包括自动生成电子邮件、文档和其他通讯内容，也包括对用户提供文本的编辑、批评、摘要和翻译等。“写作”在工作场景中是最常见的使用场景，2025 年 6 月平均占工作相关消息的 40 % 40 % 40%40 \% 。大约三分之二的所有“写作”消息是要求 ChatGPT 修改用户文本（编辑、批评、翻译等），而不是从头创建新文本。大约 10 % 10 % 10%10 \% 的所有消息是请求辅导或教学的，表明教育是 ChatGPT 的一个关键使用场景。
Two of our findings stand in contrast to other work. First, we find the share of messages related to computer coding is relatively small: only 4.2 % 4.2 % 4.2%4.2 \% of ChatGPT messages are related to computer programming, compared to 33 % 33 % 33%33 \% of work-related Claude conversations Handa et al. (2025). 8 8 ^(8){ }^{8} Second, we find the share of messages related to companionship or social-emotional issues is fairly small: only 1.9 % 1.9 % 1.9%1.9 \% of ChatGPT messages are on the topic of Relationships and Personal Reflection and 0.4 % 0.4 % 0.4%0.4 \% are related
我们的两项发现与其他研究形成对比。首先，我们发现与计算机编程相关的消息比例相对较小：只有 4.2 % 4.2 % 4.2%4.2 \% 的 ChatGPT 消息与计算机编程有关，而 Handa et al. (2025) 的工作相关 Claude 对话中该比例为 33 % 33 % 33%33 \% 。其次，我们发现与陪伴或社会情感问题相关的消息比例也相当小：只有 1.9 % 1.9 % 1.9%1.9 \% 的 ChatGPT 消息属于“人际关系与个人反思”主题，且 0.4 % 0.4 % 0.4%0.4 \% 与此相关。
to Games and Role Play. In contrast, Zao-Sanders (2025) estimates that Therapy/Companionship is the most prevalent use case for generative AI. 9 9 ^(9){ }^{9}
到游戏和角色扮演。相反，Zao-Sanders (2025) 估计治疗/陪伴是生成式 AI 最普遍的使用场景。 9 9 ^(9){ }^{9}
We also document several important facts about demographic variation in ChatGPT usage. First, we show evidence that the gender gap in ChatGPT usage has likely narrowed considerably over time, and may have closed completely. In the few months after ChatGPT was released about 80 % 80 % 80%80 \% of active users had typically masculine first names. 10 10 ^(10){ }^{10} However, that number declined to 48 % 48 % 48%48 \% as of June 2025, with active users slightly more likely to have typically feminine first names. Second, we find that nearly half of all messages sent by adults were sent by users under the age of 26, although age gaps have narrowed somewhat in recent months. Third, we find that ChatGPT usage has grown relatively faster in low- and middle-income countries over the last year. Fourth, we find that educated users and users in highly-paid professional occupations are substantially more likely to use ChatGPT for work.
我们还记录了有关 ChatGPT 使用中人口统计差异的若干重要事实。首先，我们的证据表明 ChatGPT 使用中的性别差距很可能随着时间大幅缩小，甚至可能已完全消失。在 ChatGPT 发布后的几个月里，大约 80 % 80 % 80%80 \% 的活跃用户通常使用男性化的名字。 10 10 ^(10){ }^{10} 然而，截至 2025 年 6 月，该比例下降至 48 % 48 % 48%48 \% ，活跃用户中使用女性化名字者略微占优。第二，我们发现几乎一半由成年人发送的所有消息是由 26 岁以下的用户发送的，尽管近几个月年龄差距有所缩小。第三，我们发现在过去一年中，ChatGPT 在低收入和中等收入国家的增长相对更快。第四，我们发现受过高等教育的用户和从事高薪专业职业的用户更有可能将 ChatGPT 用于工作。
We introduce a new taxonomy to classify messages according to the kind of output the user is seeking, using a simple rubric that we call Asking, Doing, or Expressing. 11 11 ^(11){ }^{11} Asking is when the user is seeking information or clarification to inform a decision, corresponding to problem-solving models of knowledge work (e.g., Garicano (2000); Garicano and Rossi-Hansberg (2006); Carnehl and Schneider (2025); Ide and Talamas (2025)). Doing is when the user wants to produce some output or perform a particular task, corresponding to classic task-based models of work (e.g., Autor et al. (2003)). Expressing is when the user is expressing views or feelings but not seeking any information or action. We estimate that about 49 % 49 % 49%49 \% of messages are Asking, 40 % 40 % 40%40 \% are Doing, and 11 % 11 % 11%11 \% are Expressing. However, as of July 2025 about 56 % 56 % 56%56 \% of work-related messages are classified as Doing (e.g., performing job tasks), and nearly three-quarters of those are Writing tasks. The relative frequency of writingrelated conversations is notable for two reasons. First, writing is a task that is common to nearly all white-collar jobs, and good written communication skills are among the top “soft” skills demanded by employers (National Association of Colleges and Employers, 2024). Second, one distinctive feature of generative AI, relative to other information technologies, is its ability to produce long-form outputs such as writing and software code.
我们引入了一个新的分类法，用于根据用户所寻求的输出类型对消息进行分类，使用我们称之为“询问（Asking）”、“执行（Doing）”或“表达（Expressing）”的简单评分标准。 11 11 ^(11){ }^{11} “询问”是指用户寻求信息或澄清以便做出决策，对应于以解决问题为导向的知识型工作模型（例如 Garicano (2000); Garicano and Rossi-Hansberg (2006); Carnehl and Schneider (2025); Ide and Talamas (2025)）。“执行”是指用户想要生成某些输出或执行特定任务，对应于经典的基于任务的工作模型（例如 Autor et al. (2003)）。“表达”是指用户在表达观点或情感，但并不寻求任何信息或行动。我们估计约有 49 % 49 % 49%49 \% 的消息属于“询问”， 40 % 40 % 40%40 \% 属于“执行”， 11 % 11 % 11%11 \% 属于“表达”。然而，截至 2025 年 7 月，大约 56 % 56 % 56%56 \% 的与工作相关的消息被归类为“执行”（例如，执行工作任务），且其中近四分之三是写作任务。写作相关对话的相对频率值得注意，原因有两个。 首先，写作是几乎所有白领工作中常见的任务，良好的书面沟通能力是雇主最看重的“软”技能之一（National Association of Colleges and Employers，2024）。其次，与其他信息技术相比，生成式 AI 的一个显著特征是其能够生成长篇输出，例如写作和软件代码。
We also map message content to work activities using the Occupational Information Network (O*NET), a survey of job characteristics supported by the U.S. Department of Labor. We find that about 81 % 81 % 81%81 \% of work-related messages are associated with two broad work activities: 1) obtaining, documenting, and interpreting information; and 2) making decisions, giving advice, solving problems, and thinking creatively. Additionally, we find that the work activities associated with ChatGPT usage are highly similar across very different kinds of occupations. For example, the work activities Getting Information and Making Decisions and Solving Problems are in the top five of message frequency in nearly all occupations, ranging from management and business to STEM to administrative and sales occupations.
我们还使用由美国劳工部支持的职业信息网络（O*NET）将消息内容映射到工作活动。我们发现，大约 81 % 81 % 81%81 \% 的与工作相关的消息与两类广泛的工作活动相关：1）获取、记录和解释信息；以及 2）做出决策、提供建议、解决问题和进行创造性思考。此外，我们发现与 ChatGPT 使用相关的工作活动在各种不同类型的职业中高度相似。例如，获取信息和做出决策与解决问题这类工作活动在几乎所有职业的信息消息频率排名前五，涵盖管理与商业、STEM 领域以至行政与销售职业。
Overall, we find that information-seeking and decision support are the most common ChatGPT use cases in most jobs. This is consistent with the fact that almost half of all ChatGPT usage is either Practical Guidance or Seeking Information. We also show that Asking is growing faster than
总体而言，我们发现信息搜索和决策支持是大多数职业中最常见的 ChatGPT 使用场景。这与几乎一半的 ChatGPT 使用属于“实用指导”或“寻求信息”的事实相一致。我们还显示出“询问”增长速度快于
Doing, and that Asking messages are consistently rated as having higher quality both by a classifier that measures user satisfaction and from direct user feedback.
“执行”，并且“询问”消息在质量上持续被评为更高——这一点既由衡量用户满意度的分类器体现，也由直接的用户反馈证明。
How does ChatGPT provide economic value, and for whom is its value the greatest? We argue that ChatGPT likely improves worker output by providing decision support, which is especially important in knowledge-intensive jobs where better decision-making increases productivity (Deming, 2021; Caplin et al., 2023). This explains why Asking is relatively more common for educated users who are employed in highly-paid, professional occupations. Our findings are most consistent with Ide and Talamas (2025), who develop a model where AI agents can serve either as co-workers that produce output or as co-pilots that give advice and improve the productivity of human problem-solving.
ChatGPT 如何提供经济价值？其价值对谁最大？我们认为 ChatGPT 很可能通过提供决策支持来提高工作者产出，这在知识密集型工作中尤为重要，因为更好的决策会提升生产率（Deming, 2021；Caplin et al., 2023）。这也解释了为何受过教育且从事高薪专业职业的用户中“询问”相对更常见。我们的发现与 Ide 和 Talamas (2025) 的结论最为一致：他们构建的模型表明，AI 代理可以作为产出型的共事者，也可以作为提供建议并提升人类问题解决生产率的副驾驶。

2 What is ChatGPT?
2 ChatGPT 是什么？

Here we give a simplified overview of LLMs and chatbots. For more precise details, refer to the papers and system cards that OpenAI has released with each model e.g., (OpenAI, 2023, 2024a, 2025b). A chatbot is a statistical model trained to generate a text response given some text input, so as to maximize the “quality” of that response, where the quality is measured with a variety of metrics.
这里我们对 LLMs 和聊天机器人做一个简明概述。有关更精确的细节，请参阅 OpenAI 随每个模型发布的论文和系统卡，例如 (OpenAI, 2023, 2024a, 2025b)。聊天机器人是一种统计模型，训练目的是在给定文本输入时生成文本回应，以最大化该回应的“质量”，而质量通过多种指标来衡量。
In a prototypical interaction, a user submits a plain-text message (“prompt”) and ChatGPT returns the message (“response”) generated from an underlying LLM. A large set of additional features have been added to ChatGPT -including the possibility for the LLM to search the web or external databases, and generate images based on text-but the exchange of text-based messages remains the most typical interaction.
在典型交互中，用户提交一条纯文本消息（“提示”），ChatGPT 返回由底层 LLM 生成的消息（“回应”）。ChatGPT 已增加了大量附加功能——包括让 LLM 搜索网络或外部数据库、以及根据文本生成图像的可能性——但基于文本的消息交换仍然是最典型的交互方式。
Since its launch ChatGPT has used a variety of different underlying LLMs e.g., GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4o, o1, o3, and GPT-5. 12 12 ^(12){ }^{12} In addition there are occasional updates to the model’s weights and to the model’s system prompt (text instructions sent to the model along with all the queries).
自推出以来，ChatGPT 使用了多种不同的底层 LLM，例如 GPT-3.5、GPT-4、GPT-4o、o1、o3 和 GPT-5。 12 12 ^(12){ }^{12} 另外，模型的权重和模型的系统提示（随所有查询一并发送给模型的文本指令）也会不时更新。
An LLM can be thought of as a function from a string of words to a probability distribution over the set of all possible words (more precisely, “tokens,” which very roughly correspond to words 13 13 ^(13){ }^{13} ). The functions are implemented with deep neural nets, typically with a transformer architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017), parameterized with billions of model “weights”. We will refer to all of ChatGPT’s models as language models, though most can additionally process tokens representing images, audio, or other media.
可以将一个 LLM 理解为一个函数：它将一个单词串映射到所有可能单词集合上的一个概率分布（更准确地说，是映射到“token”，这些大致对应于单词 13 13 ^(13){ }^{13} ）。这些函数由深度神经网络实现，通常采用 transformer 架构（Vaswani et al., 2017），由数十亿个模型“权重”参数化。我们将把所有 ChatGPT 的模型统称为语言模型，尽管大多数模型还可以额外处理表示图像、音频或其他媒体的 token。
The weights in an LLM-based chatbot are often trained in two stages, commonly called “pretraining” and “post-training”. In the first stage (“pre-training”), the LLMs are trained to predict the next word in a string, given the preceding words, over an enormous corpus of text. At that point the models are purely predictors of the likelihood of the next word given a prior context, and as such they have a relatively narrow application. In the second stage (“post-training”), the models are trained to produce words that comprise “good” responses to some prompt. This stage often consists of a variety of different strategies: fine-tuning on a dataset of queries and ideal responses, reinforcement learning against another model that is trained to grade the quality of a response (Ouyang et al., 2022), or reinforcement learning against a function that knows the true response to queries (OpenAI (2024b),
基于 LLM 的聊天机器人的权重通常分两个阶段训练，通常称为“预训练”和“后训练”。在第一阶段（“预训练”），LLMs 在大量文本语料上学习在给定前文的情况下预测序列中的下一个词。此时模型纯粹是基于先前上下文预测下一个词出现概率的预测器，因此其应用相对狭窄。在第二阶段（“后训练”），模型被训练以生成构成对某个提示的“好”回复的词语。该阶段通常由多种不同策略组成：在查询与理想回复的数据集上进行微调、针对另一个被训练用于评估回复质量的模型进行强化学习（Ouyang et al., 2022），或针对知道查询真实回答的函数进行强化学习（OpenAI (2024b),
Lambert et al. (2024)). This second stage also typically includes a number of “safety” constraints to avoid certain classes of response, especially those which are deemed harmful or dangerous (OpenAI, 2025a).
Lambert et al. (2024)）。这一第二阶段通常还包括若干“安全”约束以避免某些类别的回复，尤其是被认为有害或危险的回复（OpenAI, 2025a）。
This two-stage process has a common statistical interpretation: the first stage teaches the model a latent representation of the world; the second stage fits a function using that representation (Bengio et al., 2014). Pre-training the model to predict the next word effectively teaches the model a lowdimensional representation of text, representing only the key semantic features, and therefore rendering the prompt-response problem tractable with a reasonable set of training examples.
这个两阶段过程有一个常见的统计学解释：第一阶段教会模型对世界的潜在表示；第二阶段使用该表示来拟合函数（Bengio et al., 2014）。通过预训练让模型预测下一个单词，实际上是教会模型对文本的低维表示，只表示关键的语义特征，因此使得在合理数量的训练示例下提示-响应问题变得可处理。
Two common ways of evaluating chatbots are with benchmarks (batteries of questions with known answers, e.g. Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding (Hendrycks et al., 2021)) and comparisons of human preferences over two alternative responses to the same message (e.g. Chatbot Arena (Chiang et al., 2024)).
评估聊天机器人的两种常见方法是使用基准测试（具有已知答案的问题集，例如 Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding (Hendrycks et al., 2021)）和比较人类对同一消息的两种备选响应的偏好（例如 Chatbot Arena (Chiang et al., 2024)）。

3 Data and Privacy
3 数据与隐私

In this section, we describe the data used in the paper and the privacy safeguards we implemented. No member of the research team ever saw the content of user messages, and all analyses were conducted in accordance with OpenAI’s Privacy Policy (OpenAI, 2025c).
在本节中，我们描述论文中使用的数据以及我们实施的隐私保障措施。研究团队的任何成员都未曾查看用户消息内容，且所有分析均按照 OpenAI 的隐私政策 (OpenAI, 2025c) 进行。
The analysis in this paper is based on the following datasets:
本文的分析基于以下数据集：
  1. Growth: total daily message volumes from consumer ChatGPT users between November 2022 and September 2025, along with basic self-reported demographic information. This dataset is primarily used in Section 4.
    增长：2022 年 11 月至 2025 年 9 月期间消费者 ChatGPT 用户的每日消息总量，以及基本的自报人口统计信息。该数据集主要用于第 4 节。
  2. Classified messages: messages classified into coarse categories.
    已分类消息：按粗略类别分类的消息。
  • Sampled from all ChatGPT users: a random sample of approximately one million deidentified messages from logged-in consumer ChatGPT users between May 2024 and June 2025. 14 14 ^(14){ }^{14} This dataset is primarily used in Section 5.
    从所有 ChatGPT 用户抽样：对 2024 年 5 月至 2025 年 6 月期间已登录的消费者 ChatGPT 用户的大约一百万条去标识消息的随机样本。 14 14 ^(14){ }^{14} 该数据集主要用于第 5 节。
  • Sampled from a subset of ChatGPT users: two random samples of messages sent between May 2024 and July 2025 by a subset of consumer ChatGPT users (one sample at the conversation level, one sample at the user level). 15 15 ^(15){ }^{15} These datasets are primarily used in Section 6.
    从一部分 ChatGPT 用户中抽样：对 2024 年 5 月至 2025 年 7 月期间由部分消费者 ChatGPT 用户发送的消息进行了两次随机抽样（一次在会话层面抽样，一次在用户层面抽样）。 15 15 ^(15){ }^{15} 这些数据集主要用于第 6 节。
  1. Employment: aggregated employment and education categories based on publicly available data for a subset of consumer ChatGPT users. This data is only used in Section 6.
    职业：基于公开可得数据对一部分消费者 ChatGPT 用户进行的汇总职业和教育类别划分。该数据仅在第 6 节中使用。
We describe the contents of each dataset, the sampling procedures that produced them, and the privacy protections we implemented in constructing and employing them in analysis.
我们描述了每个数据集的内容、生成它们的抽样程序，以及在构建和使用它们进行分析时实施的隐私保护措施。

3.1 Growth Dataset
3.1 增长数据集

We compiled a dataset covering all usage on consumer ChatGPT Plans (Free, Plus, Pro) since ChatGPT’s launch in November 2022. We exclude users on non-consumer plans (Business f.k.a. Teams,
我们编制了一个涵盖自 2022 年 11 月 ChatGPT 推出以来所有消费者 ChatGPT 计划（Free、Plus、Pro）使用情况的数据集。我们排除了非消费者计划（Business 原名 Teams、
Enterprise, Education).
Enterprise、Education）的用户。
For each user and day, this dataset reports the total number of messages sent by the user on that day. It also reports, for each message, de-identified user metadata, including the timestamp of their first interaction with ChatGPT, the country from which their account is registered, their subscription plan on each day, and their self-reported age (reported in coarse 5-7-year buckets to protect user privacy).
对于每个用户和每天，本数据集报告该用户当天发送的消息总数。它还报告了每条消息的去标识化用户元数据，包括他们与 ChatGPT 的首次交互时间戳、账户注册所在国家/地区、他们在每一天的订阅计划以及他们的自报年龄（为保护用户隐私以粗略的 5-7 年区间报告）。

3.2 Classified Messages
3.2 已分类的消息

To understand usage while preserving user privacy, we construct message-level datasets without any human ever reading the contents of a message. See Figure 1 for an overview of the privacy-preserving classification pipeline. Messages are categorized according to 5 different LLM-based classifiers. The classifiers are introduced in more detail in Section 5, their exact text is reproduced in Appendix A, and our validation procedure is described in Appendix B.
为了在保护用户隐私的前提下理解使用情况，我们构建了消息级别的数据集，且在任何情况下都没有人类读取消息内容。隐私保护分类管道的概览见图 1。消息根据 5 种不同的 LLM 为基础的分类器进行分类。分类器在第 5 节中有更详细的介绍，其确切文本在附录 A 中重现，我们的验证程序在附录 B 中描述。
Sampled From All ChatGPT Users. We uniformly sampled approximately 1.1 million conversations, and then sampled one message within each conversation, with the following restrictions:
从所有 ChatGPT 用户中抽样。我们均匀抽样了大约 110 万次对话，然后在每次对话中抽取一条消息，具备以下限制条件：
  1. We only include messages from May 2024 to July 2025.
    我们仅包含 2024 年 5 月至 2025 年 7 月期间的消息。
  2. We exclude conversations from users who opted out of sharing their messages for model training.
    我们排除了选择不共享其消息用于模型训练的用户的对话。
  3. We exclude users who self-report their age as under 18.
    我们排除了自报年龄低于 18 岁的用户。
  4. We exclude conversations that users have deleted and from users whose accounts have been deactivated or banned.
    我们排除了用户已删除的对话以及其账户已被停用或封禁的用户的对话。
  5. We exclude logged-out users, 16 16 ^(16){ }^{16} which represented a minority share of ChatGPT users over the sample period.
    我们排除了已登出用户， 16 16 ^(16){ }^{16} 在样本期内代表了 ChatGPT 用户的少数比例。
Our sample is drawn from a table that is itself sampled, where the sampling rate varied over time. We thus adjust our sampling weights to maintain a fixed ratio with aggregate messages sent.
我们的样本来自一个本身被抽样的表，该表的抽样率随时间变化。因此，我们调整了抽样权重以保持与发送的总消息数的固定比率。
Sampled From a Subset of ChatGPT Users. We construct two samples of classified messages from a subset of ChatGPT users (approximately 130,000 users). This sample of users does not include any users who opted out of sharing their messages for training, nor does it include users whose selfreported age is below 18, nor does it include users who have been banned or deleted their accounts.
从一部分 ChatGPT 用户抽样。我们构建了两个来自一部分 ChatGPT 用户（约 130,000 名用户）的已分类消息样本。该用户样本不包括选择不共享其消息用于训练的用户，也不包括自报年龄低于 18 岁的用户，也不包括被封禁或已删除其账户的用户。
The first sample contains classifications of 1.58 million messages from this subset of users, sampled at the conversation level (a conversation is a series of messages between the user and chatbot). This sample is constructed such that the user’s representation in the data is proportional to overall message volume. The second sample contains messages sent from this subset of users, sampled at the user level with up to six messages from each user in the group.
第一个样本包含来自该用户子集的 158 万条消息的分类，按会话层面抽样（会话是用户与聊天机器人之间的一系列消息）。该样本的构建使得用户在数据中的代表性与其总体消息量成比例。第二个样本包含来自该用户子集的消息，按用户层面抽样，每位用户最多包含该组中的六条消息。
Figure 1: Figure 1: Illustration of Privacy-Preserving Automated Classification Pipeline (Synthetic Example). Messages are first stripped of PII via an internal LLM-based tool called Privacy Filter. Then they are classified by LLM-based automated classifiers, described in detail in Appendices A and B. Humans do not see raw messages or PII-scrubbed messages, only the final classifications of messages.
图 1：隐私保护的自动化分类流程示意图（示例）。消息首先通过名为 Privacy Filter 的内部基于 LLM 的工具剥离个人识别信息（PII）。然后由基于 LLM 的自动分类器进行分类，详见附录 A 和 B。人工不会查看原始消息或已去除 PII 的消息，只能看到消息的最终分类结果。
Privacy via Automated Classifiers. No one looked at the content of messages while conducting analysis for this paper. All analysis of message content was performed via automated LLM-based classifiers run on de-identified and PII-scrubbed message data (see Figure 1). The messages are first scrubbed of PII using an internal LLM-based tool, 17 17 ^(17){ }^{17} and then classified according to classifiers defined over a controlled label space - the most precise classifier we use on the message-level data set is the O*NET Intermediate Work Activities taxonomy, which we augment to end up with 333 categories. We introduce technical and procedural frictions that prevent accidental access to the underlying text (for example, interfaces that do not render message text to researchers).
通过自动分类器保障隐私。本文的分析过程中无人查看消息内容。所有对消息内容的分析均通过在去标识化并去除 PII 的消息数据上运行的基于 LLM 的自动分类器完成（见图 1）。消息首先使用内部基于 LLM 的工具 17 17 ^(17){ }^{17} 去除 PII，然后根据在受控标签空间中定义的分类器进行分类——我们在消息级数据集上使用的最精细的分类器是 O*NET Intermediate Work Activities 分类法，我们对其进行了扩展，最终得到 333 个类别。我们引入了技术和流程上的阻隔以防止意外访问底层文本（例如，不向研究人员渲染消息文本的界面）。
Our classifications aim to discern the intent of a given message, and thus we include the prior 10 messages in a conversation as context. 18 18 ^(18){ }^{18} For an example, see Table 2.
我们的分类旨在辨别给定消息的意图，因此我们将对话中之前的 10 条消息作为上下文纳入。 18 18 ^(18){ }^{18} 例如，见表 2。

Table 2: Table 2: Illustration of Context-Augmented Message Classifications (Synthetic Example). The left column shows a standalone message to be classified, and the right column shows the prior context included in the classification of the message on the left.
表 2：表 2：上下文增强消息分类示例（合成示例）。左列显示待分类的独立消息，右列显示在对左侧消息进行分类时包含的先前上下文。
We truncate each message to a maximum of 5,000 characters, because long context windows could induce variability in the quality of the classification (Liu et al., 2023). We classify each message with the “gpt-5-mini” model, with the exception of Interaction Quality, which uses “gpt-5,” using the prompts listed in Appendix A.
我们将每条消息截断为最多 5,000 个字符，因为较长的上下文窗口可能会导致分类质量的可变性（Liu et al., 2023）。我们使用“gpt-5-mini”模型对每条消息进行分类，Interaction Quality 除外，后者使用“gpt-5”，并采用附录 A 中列出的提示词。
We validated each of the classification prompts by comparing model classification decisions against human-judged classifications of a sample of conversations from the publicly available WildChat dataset (Zhao et al., 2024), a set of conversations with a third-party chatbot which users affirmatively gave their assent to share publicly for research purposes. 19 19 ^(19){ }^{19} Appendix B provides detail on our validation approach and performance relative to human judgment. For additional transparency, we classify a sample of 100,000 public WildChat messages and provide those data in this paper’s replication package.
我们通过将模型的分类决策与人类对公开可用的 WildChat 数据集（Zhao et al., 2024）中样本对话的人工判断分类进行比较，来验证每个分类提示词的有效性。WildChat 是一组与第三方聊天机器人的对话，用户明确同意将其公开分享用于研究目的。 19 19 ^(19){ }^{19} 附录 B 提供了我们验证方法的详细信息以及相对于人工判断的性能。为增加透明度，我们对 100,000 条公开 WildChat 消息进行了分类，并在本文的复现包中提供了这些数据。

3.3 Employment Dataset
3.3 就业数据集

We conduct limited analyses of aggregated employment categories based on publicly available data for a sample of consumer ChatGPT users. This sample included approximately 130,000 Free, Plus, and Pro users, and the employment categories were aggregated by a vendor working through a secure Data Clean Room (DCR). For this analysis, we use the same exclusion criteria as for the message-level datasets: we exclude deactivated users, banned users, users who have opted out of training, and users whose self-reported age is under 18. Because the data was only available for a subset of users the results may not be representative of the full pool of users.
我们对基于公开可用数据的聚合就业类别进行了有限分析，样本为一部分消费者 ChatGPT 用户。该样本约包括 130,000 名 Free、Plus 和 Pro 用户，就业类别由通过安全数据清洁室（DCR）工作的供应商进行聚合。对于此分析，我们使用与消息级数据集相同的排除标准：排除已停用用户、被封禁用户、已选择退出训练的用户，以及自报年龄低于 18 岁的用户。由于数据仅对部分用户可用，结果可能不代表全部用户群体。
Description. The employment data, which is aggregated from publicly available sources, includes industry, occupations coarsened to O*NET categories, seniority level, company size, and education information that is limited to the degree attained. A vendor working within a DCR procured this dataset, restricted us to running only aggregated queries against it through the DCR, and deleted it upon the study’s completion.
说明：该就业数据来自公开可用来源的聚合，包含行业、按 O*NET 类别粗化的职业、资历级别、公司规模以及仅限于所获学位的教育信息。一个在 DCR 内工作的供应商获取了该数据集，限制我们只能通过 DCR 对其运行聚合查询，并在研究完成后删除了该数据集。
Privacy via a Data Clean Room. We never directly accessed user-level demographic records. All analysis of employment data was executed exclusively within a secure DCR that permits only pre-approved aggregate computations across independently held datasets; neither party can view or export the other party’s underlying records. We governed the DCR with strict protocols: To execute any query that touched the external demographic data, we first obtained explicit sign-off from a committee of 6 coauthors and then submitted the notebook to our data partner for approval; only approved notebooks could run in the DCR (see Figure 2).
通过数据清洗室实现隐私保护。我们从未直接访问用户级别的人口统计记录。所有关于就业数据的分析均在一个安全的 DCR 中独立执行，该 DCR 仅允许对独立持有的数据集进行预先批准的聚合计算；任一方均无法查看或导出对方的底层记录。我们以严格协议管理该 DCR：要执行任何涉及外部人口统计数据的查询，首先须获得由 6 名合著者组成委员会的明确签署，然后将 notebook 提交给我们的数据合作方审批；只有获批的 notebook 才能在 DCR 中运行（见图 2）。
Our partner enforced strict aggregation limits: they only approved code that returned cells meeting a threshold of 100 users. Consequently, no individual rows or narrowly defined categories were ever visible to researchers. For example, if 99 users had the occupation “anesthesiologist,” any occupationlevel output would place those users into a “suppressed” category, or place these observations in a coarsened category (e.g. “medical professionals”) rather than reporting a separate cell of anesthesiologists.
我们的合作方实施了严格的聚合限制：他们仅批准返回满足 100 名用户阈值的单元格的代码。因此，研究人员从未看到任何单行或定义狭窄的类别。例如，如果 99 名用户的职业为 “anesthesiologist”，任何按职业的输出都会将这些用户归入“已屏蔽”类别，或将这些观测合并到更粗的类别（例如 “medical professionals”）中，而不是报告单独的 anesthesiologists 单元格。
Figure 2: Figure 2: Illustration of Aggregated Employment Category Analysis via a Data Clean Room. All queries run in the Data Clean Room must be approved by our data partner, enforcing a strict aggregation threshold (100 observations). As a result, researchers cannot access user-level employment data, only aggregated employment categories.
图 2：通过数据清洗室进行汇总就业类别分析的示意图。所有在数据清洗室中运行的查询均须经我们的数据合作方批准，并强制执行严格的聚合阈值（100 个观测值）。因此，研究人员无法访问用户级别的就业数据，仅能获取汇总的就业类别。

3.4 Summarizing Our Approach to Privacy
3.4 我们的隐私方法概述

We took measures to safeguard user privacy at every stage of analysis. To summarize, the key elements of our approach are:
我们在分析的每个阶段都采取了措施以保护用户隐私。概括而言，我们方法的关键要素包括：
Automated classification of messages. In the course of analysis, no one ever looked directly at the content of user messages: all of our analysis of the content of user messages is done through output of automated classifiers run on de-identified and PII-scrubbed usage data. Aggregated employment data via a data clean room. We analyze and report aggregated employment data through a secure data clean room environment: no one on the research team had direct access to user-level demographic data and none of our analyses report aggregates for groups with less than 100 users.
消息的自动分类。在分析过程中，没人直接查看用户消息的内容：我们对用户消息内容的所有分析均通过在去标识化并删除 PII 的使用数据上运行的自动分类器输出完成。通过数据清洗室提供的汇总就业数据。我们在安全的数据清洗室环境中分析并报告汇总的就业数据：研究团队中无人可直接访问用户级别的人口统计数据，且我们的任何分析均不报告少于 100 名用户的组的聚合数据。
In following these measures, we aim to match or exceed the privacy protection precedents set by other social scientists studying chatbots and those linking digital platform data to external sources.
在遵循这些措施时，我们的目标是达到或超越其他研究聊天机器人的社会科学家以及将数字平台数据与外部来源链接的研究者所设立的隐私保护先例。
We follow the precedent established in recent analyses of chatbot conversations (Phang et al. (2025), Eloundou et al. (2025), Handa et al. (2025), Tomlinson et al. (2025)) that rely on automated classification rather than human inspection of raw transcripts. In particular, Phang et al. (2025)'s study of affective use of ChatGPT and Eloundou et al. (2025) investigation of first-person fairness in chatbots both analyze ChatGPT message content via automated classifiers and emphasize classifierbased labeling as a scalable, privacy-preserving approach. Anthropic’s Handa et al. (2025) used a similar approach: their Clio methodology applies automated classifiers to large collections of conversations, classifying conversations into thousands of topics, and in their appendix they describe manual validation on sampled conversations (100 user conversations flagged for review and 100 randomly sampled calibrations). Like Eloundou et al., we validate our classifiers using WildChat, a public dataset of user conversations.
我们遵循近期关于聊天机器人对话分析中确立的先例（Phang et al. (2025)、Eloundou et al. (2025)、Handa et al. (2025)、Tomlinson et al. (2025)），这些研究依赖自动化分类而非对原始记录的人为检视。具体来说，Phang et al. (2025) 对 ChatGPT 情感性使用的研究和 Eloundou et al. (2025) 对聊天机器人中第一人称公平性的调查均通过自动分类器分析 ChatGPT 消息内容，并强调基于分类器的标注作为一种可扩展且保护隐私的方法。Anthropic 的 Handa et al. (2025) 采用了类似的方法：他们的 Clio 方法将自动分类器应用于大量对话集合，将对话分类到数千个主题中，并在附录中描述了对抽样对话的人工验证（100 个被标记为需审查的用户对话和 100 个随机抽样的校准对话）。与 Eloundou et al. 类似，我们使用 WildChat（一个公开的用户对话数据集）对我们的分类器进行验证。
Other papers have analyzed digital behavior and demographic data; we mention a few relevant precedents here. Humlum and Vestergaard (2025b) and Humlum and Vestergaard (2025a), for example, analyze large-scale surveys on chatbot use along with Danish administrative labor market data. Chetty et al. (2022) analyze de-identified Facebook friendship graphs and anonymized IRS tax records, aggregated at the zip code level.
其他论文也分析了数字行为和人口统计数据；这里提及一些相关的先例。例如，Humlum 和 Vestergaard (2025b) 以及 Humlum 和 Vestergaard (2025a) 分析了关于聊天机器人使用的大规模调查数据以及丹麦的行政劳动力市场数据。Chetty 等人 (2022) 分析了去标识化的 Facebook 友谊图谱和按邮政编码汇总的匿名 IRS 税务记录。

4 The Growth of ChatGPT
4 ChatGPT 的增长

ChatGPT was released to the public on November 30, 2022 as a “research preview,” and by December 5 it had more than one million registered users. Figure 3 reports the growth of overall weekly active users (WAU) on consumer plans over time. ChatGPT had more than 100 million logged-in WAU after one year, and almost 350 million after two years. 5 How ChatGPT is Used
5 ChatGPT 的使用方式

We next report on the content of ChatGPT conversations using a variety of different taxonomies. For each taxonomy we describe a “prompt” which defines a set of categories, and then apply an LLM to map each message to a category. Our categories often apply to the user’s intention, rather than the text of the conversation, and as such we never directly observe the ground truth. Nevertheless the classifier results can be interpreted as the best-guess inferences that a human would make: the guesses from the LLM correlate highly with human guesses from the same prompt, and we get similar qualitative results when the prompt includes a third category for “uncertain.”
接下来我们使用多种不同的分类法报告 ChatGPT 对话的内容。对于每种分类法，我们描述一个“提示”（prompt），该提示定义了一组类别，然后应用 LLM 将每条消息映射到某个类别。我们的类别常常适用于用户的意图，而不是对话文本本身，因此我们从未直接观测到真实情况。尽管如此，分类器结果可以被解读为人类会做出的最佳猜测：LLM 的猜测与基于相同提示的人类猜测高度相关，而且当提示中包含“未确定”这一第三类时，我们得到的定性结果也类似。

Reported values are moving averages of the past 90 days and are reported starting 90 days after the cohort is fully formed. Y-axis is an index normalized to the first reported value for the Q1 2023 cohort.
图 5：图 5：按注册同 cohort 划分的每周活跃用户每日发送消息数。样本仅考虑 ChatGPT 消费者套餐用户（Free、Plus、Pro）。报告值为过去 90 天的移动平均值，并从 cohort 完全形成后 90 天开始报告。Y 轴为相对于 2023 年第一季度 cohort 第一个报告值的归一化指数。

5.1 What share of ChatGPT queries are related to paid work?
5.1 有多少比例的 ChatGPT 查询与有偿工作有关？

We label each user message in our dataset based on whether it appears to be related to work, using an LLM classifier. The critical part of the prompt is as follows: 21 21 ^(21){ }^{21}
我们使用 LLM 分类器对数据集中每条用户消息进行标注，以判断其是否似乎与工作相关。提示的关键部分如下： 21 21 ^(21){ }^{21}
Does the last user message of this conversation transcript seem likely to be related to doing some work/employment? Answer with one of the following:
此会话记录中的最后一条用户消息是否很可能与从事某项工作/受雇有关？请从以下选项中选择一个回答：
(1) likely part of work (e.g., “rewrite this HR complaint”)
(1) 可能属于工作范畴（例如，“重写这份人力资源投诉”）
(0) likely not part of work (e.g., “does ice reduce pimples?”)
(0) 可能不属于工作范畴（例如，“冰能减少痘痘吗？”）
Table 1 shows that both types of queries grew rapidly between June 2024 and June 2025, however non-work-related messages grew faster: 53 % 53 % 53%53 \% of messages were not related to work in June 2024, which climbed to 73 % 73 % 73%73 \% by June 2025.
表 1 显示两类查询在 2024 年 6 月到 2025 年 6 月之间都迅速增长，然而与工作无关的消息增长更快：2024 年 6 月 53 % 53 % 53%53 \% 的消息与工作无关，到 2025 年 6 月升至 73 % 73 % 73%73 \% 。

Successive cohorts have had a higher share of non-work messages, but also within each cohort their non-work use has increased. Comparing the share among all users (black line) to the share among the earliest cohort of users (yellow line), we can see that they track very closely.
图 6 绘制了按累计注册队列分解的与工作无关消息的占比。后续队列的与工作无关消息占比更高，但在每个队列内部，其与工作无关的使用也在增加。将所有用户的占比（黑线）与最早一批用户的占比（黄线）进行比较，我们可以看到二者紧密跟随。

Figure 7 shows the composition of user messages over time. The three most common Conversation Topics are Practical Guidance, Seeking Information, and Writing, collectively accounting for about 77 % 77 % 77%77 \% of all ChatGPT conversations. Practical Guidance has remained constant at roughly 29 % 29 % 29%29 \% of overall usage. Writing has declined from 36 % 36 % 36%36 \% of all usage in July 2024 to 24 % 24 % 24%24 \% a year later. Seeking Information has grown from 14 % 14 % 14%14 \% to 24 % 24 % 24%24 \% of all usage over the same period. The share of Technical Help declined from 12% from all usage in July 2024 to around 5% a year later - this may be because the use of LLMs for programming has grown very rapidly through the API (outside of ChatGPT), for AI assistance in code editing and for autonomous programming agents (e.g. Codex). Multimedia grew from 2 % 2 % 2%2 \% to just over 7%, with a large spike in April 2025 after ChatGPT released new imagegeneration capabilities: the spike attenuated but the elevated level has persisted.
图 7 显示了随时间变化的用户消息构成。三大最常见的对话主题是 Practical Guidance、Seeking Information 和 Writing，合计约占所有 ChatGPT 对话的 77 % 77 % 77%77 \% 。Practical Guidance 在总体使用中大致保持在 29 % 29 % 29%29 \% 的恒定水平。Writing 从 2024 年 7 月占所有使用的 36 % 36 % 36%36 \% 下降到一年后的 24 % 24 % 24%24 \% 。Seeking Information 在同一时期内从 14 % 14 % 14%14 \% 增长到 24 % 24 % 24%24 \% 的份额。Technical Help 的比例从 2024 年 7 月占所有使用的 12% 下降到一年后的约 5%——这可能是因为通过 API 在编程方面使用 LLMs 增长非常快（在 ChatGPT 之外），用于代码编辑的 AI 辅助以及自主编程代理（例如 Codex）。Multimedia 从 2 % 2 % 2%2 \% 增长到略高于 7%，在 2025 年 4 月 ChatGPT 发布新的图像生成功能后出现大幅峰值：峰值有所减弱但较高的水平持续存在。

Technical Help has declined from 18% of all work-related messages in July 2024 to just over 10% in July 2025.

数据显示，大多数用户与 ChatGPT 的写作对话是要求修改用户输入，而不是从头创造新内容。教育是 ChatGPT 的一个主要使用场景。所有用户消息中有 10.2 % 10.2 % 10.2%10.2 \% ，以及实用指导消息中有 36 % 36 % 36%36 \% ，是针对辅导或教学的请求。另一大部分——总计 8.5 % 8.5 % 8.5%8.5 \% ，在实用指导中占 30 % 30 % 30%30 \% ——是关于各种主题的一般操作性建议。技术帮助包括计算机编程（4.2% 的消息）、数学计算（3%）和数据分析（0.4%）。在自我表达主题方面，只有 2.4 % 2.4 % 2.4%2.4 \% 的所有 ChatGPT 消息与人际关系与个人反思（1.9%）或游戏与角色扮演（0.4%）有关。
While users can seek information and advice from traditional web search engines as well as from ChatGPT, the ability to produce writing, software code, spreadsheets, and other digital products distinguishes generative AI from existing technologies. ChatGPT is also more flexible than web search even for traditional applications like Seeking Information and Practical Guidance, because users receive customized responses (e.g., tailored workout plans, new product ideas, ideas for fantasy football team names) that represent newly generated content or novel modification of user-provided content and follow-up requests.
虽然用户可以像向传统网络搜索引擎一样向 ChatGPT 寻求信息和建议，但能够生成文章、软件代码、电子表格及其他数字产品的能力，使生成式 AI 有别于现有技术。即便是在“寻求信息”和“实用指导”等传统应用上，ChatGPT 也比网络搜索更具灵活性，因为用户会收到定制化回答（例如，量身定制的健身计划、新产品创意、幻想橄榄球队名的创意等），这些回答代表新生成的内容或对用户提供内容及后续请求的新颖修改。

5.3 User Intent
5.3 用户意图

Existing studies of the economic impacts of generative AI focus almost exclusively on the potential for AI to perform workplace tasks, either augmenting or automating human labor (e.g. Eloundou et al. (2025), Handa et al. (2025), Tomlinson et al. (2025)). However, generative AI is a highly flexible
现有关于生成式 AI 经济影响的研究几乎完全集中于 AI 在执行职场任务上的潜力，无论是增强还是自动化人类劳动（例如 Eloundou et al. (2025)、Handa et al. (2025)、Tomlinson et al. (2025)）。然而，生成式 AI 是一种高度灵活的
technology that can be used in many different ways. In order to learn more about how people seek to use generative AI at work and outside of work, we introduce a classifier that is designed to measure the type of output the user hopes to receive. Specifically, we classify messages according to user intent, coding up conversations according to a simple Asking, Doing, or Expressing rubric. The critical part of our classification prompt is as follows:
技术，可以用于多种不同的方式。为了更多地了解人们在工作内外如何寻求使用生成式 AI，我们引入了一个分类器，旨在衡量用户希望获得的输出类型。具体而言，我们根据用户意图对消息进行分类，按照一个简单的“询问（Asking）”、“执行（Doing）”或“表达（Expressing）”的框架对对话进行编码。我们分类提示的关键部分如下：
Intent
意图		 Prompt
提示
Asking
提问		 Asking is seeking information or advice that will help the user be better informed or make better decisions, either at work, at school, or in their personal life. (e.g. "Who was president after Lincoln?", "How do I create a budget for this quarter?", "What was the inflation rate last year?", "What's the difference between correlation and causation?", "What should I look for when choosing a health plan during open enrollment?").
提问是寻求信息或建议，帮助用户在工作、学校或个人生活中获得更好的信息或做出更好的决策。（例如：“林肯之后谁当总统？”，“我如何为本季度制定预算？”，“去年的通货膨胀率是多少？”，“相关性和因果关系有什么区别？”，“在开放注册期间选择健康计划时我应该注意什么？”）。
Doing
执行		 Doing messages request that ChatGPT perform tasks for the user. User is drafting an email, writing code, etc. Classify messages as "doing" if they include requests for output that is created primarily by the model. (e.g. "Rewrite this email to make it more formal", "Draft a report summarizing the use cases of ChatGPT", "Produce a project timeline with milestones and risks in a table", "Extract companies, people, and dates from this text into CSV.","Write a Dockerfile and a minimal docker-compose.yml for this app.")
执行类消息要求 ChatGPT 为用户执行任务。用户正在起草电子邮件、编写代码等。如果消息包含模型主要生成输出的请求，则将其归类为“执行”。（例如：“重写这封邮件使其更正式”，“起草一份总结 ChatGPT 用例的报告”，“制作一个包含里程碑和风险的项目时间表表格”，“将文本中的公司、人物和日期提取为 CSV”，“为此应用编写 Dockerfile 和最小的 docker-compose.yml。”）
Expressing
表达		 Expressing statements are neither asking for information, nor for the chatbot to perform a task.
表达类陈述既不是在询问信息，也不是要求聊天机器人执行某项任务。
Intent Prompt Asking Asking is seeking information or advice that will help the user be better informed or make better decisions, either at work, at school, or in their personal life. (e.g. "Who was president after Lincoln?", "How do I create a budget for this quarter?", "What was the inflation rate last year?", "What's the difference between correlation and causation?", "What should I look for when choosing a health plan during open enrollment?"). Doing Doing messages request that ChatGPT perform tasks for the user. User is drafting an email, writing code, etc. Classify messages as "doing" if they include requests for output that is created primarily by the model. (e.g. "Rewrite this email to make it more formal", "Draft a report summarizing the use cases of ChatGPT", "Produce a project timeline with milestones and risks in a table", "Extract companies, people, and dates from this text into CSV.","Write a Dockerfile and a minimal docker-compose.yml for this app.") Expressing Expressing statements are neither asking for information, nor for the chatbot to perform a task.| Intent | Prompt | | :--- | :--- | | Asking | Asking is seeking information or advice that will help the user be better informed or make better decisions, either at work, at school, or in their personal life. (e.g. "Who was president after Lincoln?", "How do I create a budget for this quarter?", "What was the inflation rate last year?", "What's the difference between correlation and causation?", "What should I look for when choosing a health plan during open enrollment?"). | | Doing | Doing messages request that ChatGPT perform tasks for the user. User is drafting an email, writing code, etc. Classify messages as "doing" if they include requests for output that is created primarily by the model. (e.g. "Rewrite this email to make it more formal", "Draft a report summarizing the use cases of ChatGPT", "Produce a project timeline with milestones and risks in a table", "Extract companies, people, and dates from this text into CSV.","Write a Dockerfile and a minimal docker-compose.yml for this app.") | | Expressing | Expressing statements are neither asking for information, nor for the chatbot to perform a task. |
Conceptually, Doing conversations are delivering output that can be plugged into a production process, while Asking conversations support decision-making but do not produce output directly, and Expressing conversations have little or no economic content.
从概念上讲，Doing 类型的对话会产生可直接投入生产过程的输出，Asking 类型的对话用于支持决策但不会直接产生输出，而 Expressing 类型的对话几乎没有或完全没有经济内容。
Figure 10 shows the share of messages by each intent type in our sample. 49 % 49 % 49%49 \% of user messages are Asking, 40 % 40 % 40%40 \% are Doing, and 11 % 11 % 11%11 \% are Expressing. The figure also shows the relationship with our Topic classification: the two taxonomies are correlated but not redundant: Asking queries are more likely to be Practical Guidance and Seeking Information. Doing queries are disproportionately Writing and Multimedia. Expressing queries are disproportionately Self-Expression. However, the overlap is imperfect. For example, within the Practical Guidance topic, an Asking message might be advice about how to recover from a sports injury given a user’s personal history, while a Doing message might request ChatGPT to produce a customized recovery and training plan that could be printed or saved. Within Technical Help, an Asking message might request help understanding how to debug some code, while a Doing message might ask ChatGPT to write code for the user directly.
图 10 显示了样本中按意图类型划分的消息占比。 49 % 49 % 49%49 \% 的用户消息属于 Asking， 40 % 40 % 40%40 \% 属于 Doing， 11 % 11 % 11%11 \% 属于 Expressing。该图还展示了与我们的主题分类之间的关系：两种分类法相关但不冗余：Asking 查询更可能属于 Practical Guidance 和 Seeking Information。Doing 查询在 Writing 和 Multimedia 中所占比例偏高。Expressing 查询在 Self-Expression 中所占比例偏高。然而，两者的重合并不完美。例如，在 Practical Guidance 主题下，Asking 消息可能是基于用户个人病史询问如何从运动损伤中恢复的建议，而 Doing 消息可能要求 ChatGPT 生成一个可打印或保存的定制恢复与训练计划。在 Technical Help 中，Asking 消息可能是请求帮助理解如何调试某段代码，而 Doing 消息可能直接请求 ChatGPT 为用户编写代码。

Doing constitutes nearly 56 % 56 % 56%56 \% of work-related queries, compared to 35 % 35 % 35%35 \% for Asking and 9 % 9 % 9%9 \% for Expressing. Nearly 35 % 35 % 35%35 \% of all work-related queries are Doing messages related to Writing. Doing and Asking comprise equal shares of Technical Help queries.
图 11 显示了仅针对与工作相关消息的 Asking/Doing/Expressing 比例。Doing 占与工作相关查询的近 56 % 56 % 56%56 \% ，相比之下 Asking 为 35 % 35 % 35%35 \% ，Expressing 为 9 % 9 % 9%9 \% 。几乎 35 % 35 % 35%35 \% 的所有与工作相关查询是与写作相关的 Doing 消息。Doing 与 Asking 在技术帮助查询中占比相等。

5.4 O*NET Work Activities
5.4 O*NET 工作活动

We map message content to work activities using the Occupational Information Network (ONET) Database Version 29.0, similar to Tomlinson et al (2025). ONET was developed in partnership with the U.S. Department of Labor and systematically classifies jobs according to the skills, tasks, and work activities required to perform them. O*NET associates each occupation with a set of tasks that are performed at different levels of intensity. Each task is then aggregated up to three levels of detail - 2,087 detailed work activities (DWAs), 332 intermediate work activities (IWAs), and 41 generalized work activities (GWAs).
我们使用 Occupational Information Network (ONET) 数据库 29.0 版将消息内容映射到工作活动，方法类似于 Tomlinson 等人（2025）。ONET 与美国劳工部合作开发，系统地根据完成某项工作所需的技能、任务和工作活动对职业进行分类。O*NET 将每个职业与一组在不同强度水平上执行的任务相关联。每项任务随后被汇总为三个层次的细化程度——2,087 项详细工作活动（DWAs）、332 项中级工作活动（IWAs）和 41 项通用工作活动（GWAs）。
To understand the work activities associated with ChatGPT usage, we mapped messages to one of the 332 O*NET Intermediate Work Activities (IWA), with an additional option of Ambiguous to account for situations where the user message lacked sufficient context. 22 22 ^(22){ }^{22} We then used the official
为了理解与 ChatGPT 使用相关的工作活动，我们将消息映射到 332 项 O*NET 中级工作活动（IWA）中的一项，并增加了“模糊”这一选项以处理用户消息缺乏足够上下文的情况。 22 22 ^(22){ }^{22} 然后我们使用了官方

O*NET taxonomy to map these classified IWAs to one of the Generalized Work Activities (GWA). We do not show the shares for the following GWAs as there were fewer than 100 users sending messages for each category and group them into Suppressed.
使用 O*NET 分类法将这些已分类的 IWA 映射到泛化工作活动（GWA）之一。我们未展示以下 GWA 的比例，因为每个类别的发送消息用户少于 100 人，故将其归入“已抑制”。
Figure 14 presents the share of messages that belong to each GWA, in descending order. Nearly half of all messages ( 45.2 % 45.2 % 45.2%45.2 \% ) fall under just three GWAs related to information use and manipulation: Getting Information (19.3%), Interpreting the Meaning of Information for Others (13.1%), and Documenting/Recording Information (12.8%). The next most common work activities are Providing Consultation and Advice (9.2%), Thinking Creatively (9.1%), Making Decisions and Solving Problems ( 8.5 % 8.5 % 8.5%8.5 \% ), and Working with Computers ( 4.9 % 4.9 % 4.9%4.9 \% ). These seven GWAs collectively account for 76.9 % 76.9 % 76.9%76.9 \% of all messages.
图 14 显示了属于每个 GWA 的消息比例，按降序排列。近一半的消息（ 45.2 % 45.2 % 45.2%45.2 \% ）仅属于与信息使用和处理相关的三个 GWA：获取信息 (19.3%)、为他人解读信息含义 (13.1%) 和记录/记载信息 (12.8%)。接下来最常见的工作活动是提供咨询和建议 (9.2%)、创造性思维 (9.1%)、决策与问题解决 ( 8.5 % 8.5 % 8.5%8.5 \% ) 以及与计算机相关的工作 ( 4.9 % 4.9 % 4.9%4.9 \% )。这七个 GWA 合计占所有消息的 76.9 % 76.9 % 76.9%76.9 \% 。
Figure 15 presents the distribution of GWAs for the subsample of messages we classify as workrelated. Among work-related messages, the most common GWAs are Documenting/Recording Information (18.4%), Making Decisions and Solving Problems (14.9%), Thinking Creatively (13.0%), Working with Computers (10.8%), Interpreting the Meaning of Information for Others (10.1%), Getting Information (9.3%), and Providing Consultation and Advice to Others (4.4%). These seven GWAs collectively account for nearly 81 % 81 % 81%81 \% of work-related messages. Overall, the majority of ChatGPT usage at work appears to be focused on two broad functions: 1) obtaining, documenting, and interpreting information; and 2) making decisions, giving advice, solving problems, and thinking creatively.

5.5 Quality of Interactions
5.5 交互质量

We additionally used automated classifiers to study the user’s apparent satisfaction with the chatbot’s response to their request. Our Interaction Quality classifier looks for an expression of satisfaction or dissatisfaction in the user’s subsequent message in the same conversation (if one exists), with three possible categories: Good, Bad, and Unknown. 23 23 ^(23){ }^{23}
我们还使用自动分类器来研究用户对聊天机器人对其请求的回复的明显满意度。我们的交互质量分类器在同一对话中（如果存在用户后续消息）寻找用户表达满意或不满意的迹象，分为三类：Good、Bad 和 Unknown。 23 23 ^(23){ }^{23}
Figure 16 plots the overall growth of messages in these three buckets. In late 2024 Good interactions were about three times as common as Bad interactions, but Good interactions grew much more rapidly over the next nine months, and by July 2025 they were more than four times more common.
图 16 绘制了这三类消息的总体增长情况。在 2024 年底，Good 交互大约是 Bad 交互的三倍，但在接下来的九个月中，Good 交互增长更快，到 2025 年 7 月已超过四倍。

6 Who Uses ChatGPT
6 谁在使用 ChatGPT

In this section we report basic descriptive facts about who uses consumer ChatGPT. Existing work documents variation in generative AI use by demographic groups within representative samples in the U.S. (Bick et al. (2024), Hartley et al. (2025)) and within a subset of occupations in Denmark (Humlum and Vestergaard, 2025a). All of these papers find that generative AI is used more frequently by men, young people, and those with tertiary and/or graduate education.
在本节中，我们报告关于谁使用消费者版 ChatGPT 的基本描述性事实。已有研究在美国的代表性样本中记录了生成式 AI 使用在不同人口群体间的差异（Bick et al. (2024), Hartley et al. (2025)），以及在丹麦的部分职业子集中（Humlum and Vestergaard, 2025a）。所有这些论文都发现，生成式 AI 的使用在男性、年轻人以及具有高等教育和/或研究生教育的人群中更为频繁。
We make three contributions relative to this prior literature. First, we confirm these broad demographic patterns in a global sample rather than a single country. Second, we provide more detail for selected demographics such as age, gender, and country of origin and study how gaps in each have changed over time. Third, we use a secure data clean room to analyze how ChatGPT usage varies by education and occupation.
相较于既有文献，我们有三点贡献。首先，我们在全球样本（而非单一国家）中确认了这些广泛的人口统计学模式。第二，我们对选定的人口变量（如年龄、性别和原籍国）提供了更详细的信息，并研究了这些群体差距随时间的变化。第三，我们使用安全数据清洁室分析 ChatGPT 使用在教育程度和职业间的差异。

6.1 Name Analysis
6.1 名称分析

We investigate potential variation by gender by classifying a global random sample of over 1.1 million ChatGPT users’ first names using public aggregated datasets of name-gender associations. We used the World Gender Name Dictionary, and Social Security popular names, as well as datasets of popular Brazilian and Latin American names. This methodology is similar to that in (Hofstra et al., 2020) and (West et al., 2013). Names that were not in these datasets, or were flagged as ambiguous in the datasets, or had significant disagreement amongst these datasets were classified as Unknown.
我们通过将全球随机抽样的超过 110 万名 ChatGPT 用户的名字与公开的姓名-性别关联汇总数据集进行匹配来研究性别差异的潜在变化。我们使用了 World Gender Name Dictionary、Social Security 的流行名字数据，以及巴西和拉丁美洲常用名字的数据集。该方法学与(Hofstra et al., 2020)和(West et al., 2013)中的方法相似。那些不在这些数据集中、在数据集中被标记为模糊的，或在这些数据集中存在显著分歧的名字被归类为“未知”。
Excluding Unknown, a significant share (around 80%) of the weekly active users (WAU) in the first few months after ChatGPT was released were by users with typically masculine first names. However, in the first half of 2025, we see the share of active users with typically feminine and typically masculine names reach near-parity. By June 2025 we observe active users are more likely to have typically feminine names. This suggests that gender gaps in ChatGPT usage have closed substantially over time.
在排除“未知”之后，ChatGPT 发布后最初几个月，每周活跃用户（WAU）中有相当大的一部分（约 80%）使用的是典型的男性名字。然而，在 2025 年上半年，我们看到使用典型女性名字和典型男性名字的活跃用户比例接近持平。到 2025 年 6 月，我们观察到活跃用户更可能使用典型女性名字。这表明 ChatGPT 使用中的性别差距随时间大幅缩小。
We also study differences in usage topics. Users with typically female first names are relatively more likely to send messages related to Writing and Practical Guidance. By contrast, users with typically male first names are more likely to use ChatGPT for Technical Help, Seeking Out Information, and Multimedia (e.g., modifying or creating images).
我们还研究了使用主题的差异。通常以女性名字为首名的用户更有可能发送与写作和实用指导相关的消息。相反，通常以男性名字为首名的用户更倾向于将 ChatGPT 用于技术帮助、信息检索以及多媒体（例如修改或创建图像）。

6.2 Variation by Age
6.2 按年龄的差异

A subset of users self-report their age when registering for OpenAI. Among those who self-report their age, around 46 % 46 % 46%46 \% of the messages in our dataset are accounted for by users 18-25.
一部分用户在注册 OpenAI 时会自报年龄。在那些自报年龄的用户中，我们数据集中约有 46 % 46 % 46%46 \% 的消息来自 18–25 岁的用户。
A higher share of messages are work-related for older users. Work-related messages comprised approximately 23 % 23 % 23%23 \% of messages for users under age 26 , with this share increasing with age. The one exception is users who self-attest to being 66 years-old or older, with only 16 % 16 % 16%16 \% of their classified messages being work-related. The plot below shows trends in the share of work-related messages by age group. ChatGPT usage has become less work-related over time for users of all ages.
较年长用户的消息中工作相关的比例更高。对于 26 岁以下的用户，工作相关消息约占 23 % 23 % 23%23 \% ，且随着年龄增长这一比例上升。唯一的例外是自称 66 岁或以上的用户，他们被分类为工作相关的消息仅占 16 % 16 % 16%16 \% 。下图显示了按年龄组划分的工作相关消息比例趋势。对所有年龄段用户而言，ChatGPT 的使用随时间变得不那么以工作为主。

6.3 Variation by Country
6.3 按国家的差异

We study global patterns of ChatGPT usage by measuring the proportion of weekly consumer ChatGPT users among the internet enabled population of countries with populations larger than 1 million. We also exclude countries in which ChatGPT is blocked. The figure below plots this proportion in May 2024 and May 2025 by GDP-per-capita deciles: countries are ranked by GDP-per-capita and split into ten deciles, and the x-axis shows each decile’s median GDP-per-capita (in thousands of U.S. dollars). 24 24 ^(24){ }^{24} The solid line shows the median share within each decile; the shaded band is the interquartile range ( 25 th -75 th percentile) of country values within that decile. Comparing May 2024 to May 2025, we see that the adoption of ChatGPT grew dramatically, but also that there was disproportionate growth in low to middle-income countries ( $ 10 , 000 − 40 , 000 $ 10 , 000 − 40 , 000 $10,000-40,000\$ 10,000-40,000 GDP-per-capita). Overall, we find that many low-to-middle income countries have experienced high growth in ChatGPT adoption.
我们通过测量人口超过 100 万且可接入互联网的国家中，每周使用 ChatGPT 的消费者比例来研究全球 ChatGPT 使用模式。我们也排除了被屏蔽 ChatGPT 的国家。下图按人均 GDP 十分位绘制了 2024 年 5 月和 2025 年 5 月的该比例：国家按人均 GDP 排序并分成十个十分位，x 轴显示每个十分位的中位人均 GDP（以千美元计）。 24 24 ^(24){ }^{24} 实线表示每个十分位内的中位份额；阴影带表示该十分位中国家值的四分位距（第 25 百分位至第 75 百分位）。将 2024 年 5 月与 2025 年 5 月进行比较，可以看到 ChatGPT 的采纳率大幅增长，但在低至中等收入国家（ $ 10 , 000 − 40 , 000 $ 10 , 000 − 40 , 000 $10,000-40,000\$ 10,000-40,000 人均 GDP）中增长尤为显著。总体而言，我们发现许多低至中等收入国家在 ChatGPT 采纳方面经历了较高的增长。

Educated users are much more likely to use ChatGPT for work. 37 % 37 % 37%37 \% of messages are work-related for users with less than a bachelor’s degree, compared to 46 % 46 % 46%46 \% for users with exactly a bachelor’s degree and 48 % 48 % 48%48 \% for those with some graduate education. Panel B explores variation by education in user intent. Prior to regression adjustment, the frequency of Doing messages is increasing in education. However, this pattern reverses after adjusting for other characteristics such as occupation. We regress each message share on education and occupation, controlling for the following covariates: age, whether the name was typically masculine or feminine, seniority within role, company size, and industry. (To guarantee user privacy, we coarsen all covariates to broad categories and programmatically enforce that each group has at least 100 members prior to running the regression) We add the coefficients on each education and occupation category to the unadjusted value for the reference category and compute 95 % 95 % 95%95 \% confidence intervals using the standard errors from the regression coefficients. The sample for this regression is the approximately 40,000 users of the original 130,000 sample whose publicly available occupation was not blank or consisted of strictly special characters (as determined by a classification script). Shares for each user are calculated by randomly sampling up to six conversations attributed to the user from May 2024 through July 2025.
图 23：图 22：按教育程度划分的 ChatGPT 使用差异。每个图显示未经调整与回归调整后的估计值，以及 95 % 95 % 95%95 \% 置信区间。我们将每条消息占比对教育程度和职业进行回归，并控制以下协变量：年龄、姓名通常为男性或女性、岗位资历、公司规模和行业。（为保障用户隐私，我们将所有协变量粗分类为宽泛类别，并在运行回归前以程序方式强制每个组至少有 100 名成员）我们将每个教育和职业类别的系数加到参考类别的未经调整值上，并使用回归系数的标准误计算 95 % 95 % 95%95 \% 置信区间。用于该回归的样本是原始 130,000 个样本中约 40,000 名用户，这些用户的公开职业信息非空且不全为特殊字符（由分类脚本判定）。每位用户的占比通过从 2024 年 5 月至 2025 年 7 月间随机抽取最多六个归属该用户的对话来计算。

6.5 Variation by Occupation
6.5 按职业的差异

Figure 23 presents variation in ChatGPT usage by user occupation. Due to privacy-preserving aggregation limits, we report results for the following broad occupation categories - (1) all nonprofessional occupations, including administrative, clerical, service, and blue-collar occupations; (2) computerrelated occupations; (3) engineering and science occupations; (4) management and business occupations; and (5) all other professional occupations, including law, education, and health care. 26 26 ^(26){ }^{26} As above, the left-hand side of the figure shows unadjusted comparisons and the right-hand side presents the coefficients on each occupation category from a regression of message shares on age, whether the name was typically masculine or feminine, education, occupation categories, job seniority, firm size, and industry.
图 23 展示了按用户职业划分的 ChatGPT 使用差异。由于隐私保护的聚合限制，我们报告以下宽泛职业类别的结果——(1) 所有非专业职业，包括行政、文书、服务和蓝领职业；(2) 计算机相关职业；(3) 工程与科学职业；(4) 管理与商业职业；以及 (5) 所有其他专业职业，包括法律、教育和医疗保健。 26 26 ^(26){ }^{26} 如上图所示，图的左侧显示未调整的比较，右侧则展示了将消息份额对年龄、姓名典型的性别（男性或女性）、教育、职业类别、职位资历、公司规模和行业回归后各职业类别的系数。
Users in highly paid professional and technical occupations are more likely to use ChatGPT for work. 27 27 ^(27){ }^{27} Panel A shows that the unadjusted work shares are 57 % 57 % 57%57 \% for computer-related occupations; 50 % 50 % 50%50 \% for management and business; 48 % 48 % 48%48 \% for engineering and science; 44 % 44 % 44%44 \% for other professional occupations; and only 40 % 40 % 40%40 \% for all non-professional occupations. Regression adjustment moves these figures around slightly, but the gaps by occupation remain highly statistically significant. Users in highly-paid professional occupations are more likely to send work-related messages.
高薪专业和技术职业的用户更有可能将 ChatGPT 用于工作。 27 27 ^(27){ }^{27} 面板 A 显示，未调整的工作占比对于计算机相关职业为 57 % 57 % 57%57 \% ；管理与商业为 50 % 50 % 50%50 \% ；工程与科学为 48 % 48 % 48%48 \% ；其他专业职业为 44 % 44 % 44%44 \% ；而所有非专业职业仅为 40 % 40 % 40%40 \% 。回归调整使这些数字略有变动，但按职业划分的差距仍然在统计上高度显著。高薪专业职业的用户更倾向于发送与工作相关的消息。
Because work usage is so different by occupation, we restrict the sample only to work-related messages in Panels B and C. Panel B presents the share of work-related messages that are Asking messages, by occupation. We find that users in highly paid professional occupations are more likely to use ChatGPT for Asking rather than Doing. 28 28 ^(28){ }^{28} This is especially true in scientific and technical occupations. 47 % 47 % 47%47 \% of the work-related messages sent by users employed in computer-related occupations are Asking messages, compared to only 32 % 32 % 32%32 \% for non-professional occupations. These differences shrink somewhat with regression adjustment, but remain highly statistically significant.
由于不同职业的工作使用差异很大，我们在图表 B 和 C 中将样本限制为仅与工作相关的消息。图表 B 按职业展示了工作相关消息中属于 Asking 消息的比例。我们发现，高薪专业职业的用户更倾向于将 ChatGPT 用于 Asking 而非 Doing。 28 28 ^(28){ }^{28} 在科学和技术类职业中这种情况尤为明显。 47 % 47 % 47%47 \% 由从事计算机相关职业的用户发送的工作相关消息是 Asking 消息，而非专业职业则仅为 32 % 32 % 32%32 \% 。这些差异在回归调整后有所缩小，但仍然在统计上高度显著。
Panel C presents results by conversation topic. Writing is especially common for users employed in management and business occupations, accounting for 52 % 52 % 52%52 \% of all work-related messages. Writing is also relatively common in non-professional and other professional occupations like education and health care, accounting for 50 % 50 % 50%50 \% and 49 % 49 % 49%49 \% of work-related messages respectively. Technical Help constitutes 37 % 37 % 37%37 \% of all work-related messages for users employed in computer-related occupations, compared to 16 % 16 % 16%16 \% in engineering and science and only about 8 % 8 % 8%8 \% for all other categories. Regression adjustment affects gaps by occupation only modestly. Overall there are stark differences in the distribution of conversation topics by user occupation, with work-related messages clearly focused on the core tasks in each job (e.g. Writing for management and business, Technical Help for technical occupations).
图表 C 按对话主题展示结果。写作在从事管理和商业职业的用户中尤其常见，占所有与工作相关消息的 52 % 52 % 52%52 \% 。写作在非专业和其他专业职业（如教育和医疗保健）中也相对常见，分别占与工作相关消息的 50 % 50 % 50%50 \% 和 49 % 49 % 49%49 \% 。对于从事计算机相关职业的用户，技术帮助占所有与工作相关消息的 37 % 37 % 37%37 \% ，而在工程与科学中为 16 % 16 % 16%16 \% ，在所有其他类别中仅约为 8 % 8 % 8%8 \% 。回归调整仅在职业间差距方面产生了有限影响。总体而言，不同用户职业在对话主题分布上存在明显差异，且与工作相关的消息清晰地集中于各职业的核心任务（例如管理与商业的写作、技术职业的技术帮助）。
We also present data on the most common Generalized Work Activities (GWAs) associated with each broad occupation group, as measured by 2-digit Standard Occupation Classification (SOC) codes. Table 24 presents the frequency ranking of work-related messages in each SOC code of the seven most common GWAs. 29 29 ^(29){ }^{29}
我们还展示了与每个大类职业组相关的最常见广义工作活动（GWA）数据，这些职业组以两位数的标准职业分类（SOC）代码衡量。表 24 展示了在七个最常见 GWA 中，每个 SOC 代码的与工作相关消息的频率排名。 29 29 ^(29){ }^{29}
We find remarkable similarity across occupations in how ChatGPT is used at work. For example, Making Decisions and Solving Problems is one of the two most common GWAs in every single occupation group where at least two GWAs can be reported. 30 30 ^(30){ }^{30} Similarly, Documenting and Recording Information ranks in the top four of all occupations. Thinking Creatively is ranked as the third most common GWA in 10 of the 13 occupation groups where at least three GWAs can be reported. Even though there are 41 GWAs, the seven most common overall are also the most common within each occupation group and are ranked similarly. Not surprisingly, Working with Computers is the most common GWA in computer-related occupations. In the appendix, we report the full distribution of GWA classifications intersected with two-digit SOC codes, as well as the most frequently requested GWAs out of the subset of queries which are work-related. Across all occupations, ChatGPT usage is broadly focused on seeking information and assistance with decision-making.
我们发现各职业在工作中使用 ChatGPT 的方式非常相似。例如，在每一个至少可以报告两个 GWA 的职业组中，“制定决策与解决问题”均是两个最常见的 GWA 之一 30 30 ^(30){ }^{30} 。同样，“记录与登记信息”在所有职业中均排名前四。“创造性思维”在 13 个至少可以报告三个 GWA 的职业组中有 10 个将其列为第三常见的 GWA。尽管共有 41 个 GWA，但总体上最常见的七项在各职业组内同样是最常见的，并且排名相似。不出所料，“与计算机协作”在与计算机相关的职业中最为常见。在附录中，我们报告了 GWA 分类与两位数 SOC 代码相交的完整分布，以及在属于工作相关的查询子集中最常被请求的 GWA。跨所有职业，ChatGPT 的使用主要集中在获取信息和辅助决策。

7 Conclusion
7 结论

This paper studies the rapid growth of ChatGPT, which launched in November 2022. By July 2025, ChatGPT had been used weekly by more than 700 million users, who were collectively sending more than 2.5 billion messages per day, or about 29,000 messages per second. Yet despite the rapid adoption of ChatGPT and Generative AI more broadly, little previous evidence existed on how this new technology is used and who is using it.
本文研究了于 2022 年 11 月推出的 ChatGPT 的快速增长。到 2025 年 7 月，ChatGPT 的每周活跃用户已超过 7 亿，用户每天合计发送的消息超过 25 亿条，约为每秒 29,000 条。然而，尽管 ChatGPT 及更广泛的生成式 AI 被迅速采用，关于该新技术如何被使用以及谁在使用它的证据之前仍然很少。
This is the first economics paper to use internal ChatGPT message data, and we do so while introducing a novel privacy-preserving methodology. No user messages were observed by humans during any part of the work on this paper.
这是第一篇使用内部 ChatGPT 消息数据的经济学论文，我们在引入一种新颖的隐私保护方法论的同时进行此项研究。在撰写本文的任何阶段，都没有任何用户消息被人工查看。
This paper documents eight important facts about ChatGPT. First, as of July 2025 about 70 % 70 % 70%70 \% of ChatGPT consumer queries were unrelated to work; while both work-related and non-work-related queries have been increasing, non-work queries have been increasing faster.
本文记录了关于 ChatGPT 的八个重要事实。首先，截至 2025 年 7 月，大约 70 % 70 % 70%70 \% 的 ChatGPT 消费者查询与工作无关；尽管与工作相关和非工作相关的查询都在增加，但非工作查询的增长速度更快。
Second, the three most common ChatGPT conversation topics are Practical Guidance, Writing, and Seeking Information, collectively accounting for nearly 78 % 78 % 78%78 \% of all messages. Computer Programming and Relationships and Personal Reflection account for only 4.2 % 4.2 % 4.2%4.2 \% and 1.9 % 1.9 % 1.9%1.9 \% of messages respectively.
第二，最常见的三类 ChatGPT 对话主题是实用指导、写作和寻求信息，合计占所有消息的近 78 % 78 % 78%78 \% 。计算机编程以及人际关系与个人反思分别仅占消息的 4.2 % 4.2 % 4.2%4.2 \% 和 1.9 % 1.9 % 1.9%1.9 \% 。
Third, Writing is by far the most common work use, accounting for 42 % 42 % 42%42 \% of work-related messages overall and more than half of all messages for users in management and business occupations. About two-thirds of Writing messages are requests to modify user text rather than to produce novel text from scratch.
第三，在工作用途中，写作远为常见，占所有工作相关消息的 42 % 42 % 42%42 \% ，并且在管理和商业类职业用户中占所有消息的一半以上。约三分之二的写作消息是请求修改用户已有文本，而非从头生成新的文本。
Fourth, we classify messages according to the kind of output users are seeking with a rubric we call Asking, Doing, or Expressing. About 49 % 49 % 49%49 \% of messages are users asking ChatGPT for guidance, advice, or information (Asking), 40 % 40 % 40%40 \% are requests to complete tasks that can be plugged into a process (Doing), and 1% are messages that have no clear intent (Expressing). Asking messages have grown faster than Doing messages over the last year and are rated higher quality using both a classifier that measures user satisfaction and direct user feedback.
第四，我们根据用户期望的输出类型将消息分类为“询问”（Asking），“执行”（Doing）或“表达”（Expressing）。约 49 % 49 % 49%49 \% 的消息是用户向 ChatGPT 询求指导、建议或信息（Asking）， 40 % 40 % 40%40 \% 的消息是要求完成可直接应用于流程的任务（Doing），1% 的消息没有明确意图（Expressing）。在过去一年中，询问类消息的增长速度超过执行类消息，并且在衡量用户满意度的分类器和直接用户反馈中评分更高。
Fifth, gender gaps in ChatGPT usage have likely closed substantially over time. As of July 2025, more than half of weekly active users had typically female first names. Sixth, nearly half of all messages sent by adults were from users under the age of 26. Seventh, ChatGPT usage has grown especially fast over the last year in low- and middle-income countries. Eighth, we find that users who are highly educated and working in professional occupations are more likely to use ChatGPT for work-related messages and for Asking rather than Doing messages at work.
第五，随着时间推移，ChatGPT 使用中的性别差距很可能已大幅缩小。截至 2025 年 7 月，超过半数的周活跃用户通常使用女性化的名字。第六，近一半由成年人发送的消息来自 26 岁以下的用户。第七，过去一年中，ChatGPT 在低收入和中等收入国家的增长尤为迅速。第八，我们发现受教育程度高且从事专业职业的用户更有可能在工作中使用 ChatGPT 发送与工作相关的消息，并且在工作场合更倾向于发送“询问（Asking）”类型的消息，而非“执行（Doing）”类型的消息。
Overall, our findings suggest that ChatGPT has a broad-based impact on the global economy. The fact that non-work usage is increasing faster suggests that the welfare gains from generative AI usage could be substantial. Collis and Brynjolfsson (2025) estimate that US users would have to be paid $ 98 $ 98 $98\$ 98 to forgo using generative AI for a month, implying a surplus of at least $ 97 $ 97 $97\$ 97 billion a year. Within work usage, we find that users currently appear to derive value from using ChatGPT as an advisor or research assistant, not just a technology that performs job tasks directly. Still, ChatGPT likely improves worker output by providing decision support, which is especially important in knowledge-intensive jobs where productivity is increasing in the quality of decision-making.
总体而言，我们的研究结果表明 ChatGPT 对全球经济具有广泛影响。非工作用途增长更快这一事实表明，生成式 AI 使用带来的福利增益可能是可观的。Collis 和 Brynjolfsson (2025) 估计，美国用户若要放弃使用生成式 AI 一个月，需要获得 $ 98 $ 98 $98\$ 98 的补偿，这意味着每年至少有 $ 97 $ 97 $97\$ 97 十亿美元的剩余价值。在工作用途方面，我们发现用户目前似乎从将 ChatGPT 用作顾问或研究助理中获得价值，而不仅仅是将其作为直接执行工作任务的技术。尽管如此，ChatGPT 很可能通过提供决策支持来提高工人产出，这在知识密集型岗位尤为重要，因为这些岗位的生产率随着决策质量的提高而提升。

A. 3 Conversation Topic
A. 3 会话主题

You are an internal tool that classifies a message from a user to an AI chatbot,
\leftrightarrow based on the context of the previous messages before it.
Based on the last user message of this conversation transcript and taking into
 account the examples further below as guidance, please select the capability
 the user is clearly interested in, or `other` if it is clear but not in the
\leftrightarrow list below, or `unclear` if it is hard to tell what the user even wants:
- **edit_or_critique_provided_text**: Improving or modifying text provided by the
\hookrightarrow user.
- **argument_or_summary_generation**: Creating arguments or summaries on topics not
\leftrightarrow provided in detail by the user.
- **personal_writing_or_communication**: Assisting with personal messages, emails,
\leftrightarrow or social media posts.
- **write_fiction**: Crafting poems, stories, or fictional content.
- **how_to_advice**: Providing step-by-step instructions or guidance on how to
\leftrightarrow perform tasks or learn new skills.
- **creative_ideation**: Generating ideas or suggestions for creative projects or
\hookrightarrow activities.
- **tutoring_or_teaching**: Explaining concepts, teaching subjects, or helping the
\leftrightarrow user understand educational material.
- **translation**: Translating text from one language to another.
- **mathematical_calculation**: Solving math problems, performing calculations, or
\leftrightarrow working with numerical data.
- **computer_programming**: Writing code, debugging, explaining programming
\leftrightarrow concepts, or discussing programming languages and tools.
- **purchasable_products**: Inquiries about products or services available for
\hookrightarrow purchase.
  • cooking_and_recipes: Seeking recipes, cooking instructions, or culinary ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow advice.
    cooking_and_recipes: 寻找食谱、烹饪说明或烹饪 ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 建议。
  • health_fitness_beauty_or_self_care: Seeking advice or information on physical ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow health, fitness routines, beauty tips, or self-care practices.
    health_fitness_beauty_or_self_care: 寻求关于身体 ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 健康、健身计划、美容提示或自我护理实践的建议或信息。
  • specific_info: Providing specific information typically found on websites, ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow including information about well-known individuals, current events, historical ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow events, and other facts and knowledge.
    specific_info: 提供通常可在网站上找到的具体信息， ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 包括关于知名人士、时事、历史 ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 事件以及其他事实与知识的信息。
  • greetings_and_chitchat: Casual conversation, small talk, or friendly ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow interactions without a specific informational goal.
    greetings_and_chitchat: 随意对话、寒暄或友好 ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 互动，无特定信息目标。
  • relationships_and_personal_reflection: Discussing personal reflections or ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow seeking advice on relationships and feelings.
    relationships_and_personal_reflection: 讨论个人反思或 ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 寻求关于人际关系和情感的建议。
  • games_and_role_play: Engaging in interactive games, simulations, or ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow imaginative role-playing scenarios.
    games_and_role_play: 参与互动游戏、模拟或 ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 富有想象力的角色扮演场景。
  • asking_about_the_model: Questions about the AI models capabilities or ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow characteristics.
    asking_about_the_model: 有关 AI 模型能力或 ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 特性的提问。
  • create_an_image: Requests to generate or draw new visual content based on the ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow user’s description.
    create_an_image: 根据用户 ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 的描述请求生成或绘制新的视觉内容。
  • analyze_an_image: Interpreting or describing visual content provided by the ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow user, such as photos, charts, graphs, or illustrations.
    analyze_an_image：解释或描述由 ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 用户提供的视觉内容，如照片、图表、曲线图或插图。
  • generate_or_retrieve_other_media: Creating or finding media other than text ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow or images, such as audio, video, or multimedia files.
    generate_or_retrieve_other_media：创建或查找文本 ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 或图像以外的媒体，例如音频、视频或多媒体文件。
  • data_analysis: Performing statistical analysis, interpreting datasets, or ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow extracting insights from data.
    data_analysis：进行统计分析、解释数据集，或从数据中提取 ↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 洞见。
  • unclear: If the user’s intent is not clear from the conversation.
    unclear：如果用户的意图在对话中不明确。
  • other: If the capability requested doesn’t fit any of the above categories.
    other: 如果所请求的功能不属于以上任何类别。
