# Task overview
# 任务概述

You will be given a series of messages sent by a user to a chatbot. There may be a
你将收到用户发送给聊天机器人的一系列消息。可能只有
↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow single message, or multiple messages. It’s also possible the message may be
↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 条单条消息，也可能是多条消息。消息也有可能是
↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow truncated. Your goal is to classify the user’s intent relative to a list of
↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 已被截断。你的目标是根据以下列表对用户意图进行分类
↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow Candidate Intermediate Work Activity (IWA) statements from O*NET.
↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 来自 O*NET 的候选中级工作活动 (IWA) 陈述。
Your primary task is to determine the most applicable IWA that corresponds to the
你的主要任务是根据 O*NET 中 IWA 的含义，确定最适用于
→ → rarr\rightarrow user messages, according to the meaning of the IWA in the context of O*NET
→ → rarr\rightarrow 用户消息的 IWA。
↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow taxonomy. The conversation must provide direct evidence that the user is
↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 分类法。对话必须提供直接证据，表明用户正
↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow themself trying to accomplish the IWA. It is possible that a user’s messages
↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 自身尝试完成该 IWA。用户的消息有可能
↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow may be unrelated to any IWAs or contextually ambiguous. In those cases, you can
↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 与任何 IWA 无关或在上下文上模糊不清。在这些情况下，你可以
↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow return an unknown option which will be described later on.
↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow 返回一个稍后会描述的未知选项。

Your response should be an output with the following fields:
您的响应应包含以下字段的输出：

↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow messages were most appropriately categorized for this IWA.

↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow descriptions. The only exception is if the messages are unclear or ambiguous,

↪ ↪ ↪\hookrightarrow description.

B Appendix: Classifier Validation
附录 B：分类器验证

To assess the performance of our classifiers, we compare LLM-generated labels to human labels on a publicly available corpus of chatbot conversations (WildChat; Zhao et al., 2024). Annotations were carried out by several in-house annotators 31 31 ^(31){ }^{31}.
为了评估我们分类器的性能，我们将 LLM 生成的标签与公开可用的聊天机器人对话语料库（WildChat；Zhao et al., 2024）上的人工标签进行了比较。注释由若干内部注释员 31 31 ^(31){ }^{31} 完成。
Table 5 reports agreement rates both among humans and between the model and human annotations across all tasks.
表 5 报告了所有任务中人类之间以及模型与人类注释之间的一致率。

表 5：表 5：验证总体结果。“-”表示只有两位人工标注者参与且无法使用多数表决的分类器。
For each task we report: (i) Fleiss’ κ κ kappa\kappa across human annotators; (ii) Fleiss’ κ κ kappa\kappa when treating the model as an additional annotator; (iii) the mean pairwise human-human Cohen’s κ κ kappa\kappa; and (iv) Cohen’s κ κ kappa\kappa between the model and the human plurality label. An item contributes to a statistic only if all required raters provided a nonempty label. Confidence intervals are 95 % 95 % 95%95 \% percentile intervals (2.5th and 97.5th percentiles) from a nonparametric bootstrap with 2,000 resamples.
对于每个任务，我们报告：(i) 人工标注者之间的 Fleiss’ κ κ kappa\kappa ；(ii) 将模型视为额外标注者时的 Fleiss’ κ κ kappa\kappa ；(iii) 人工—人工两两 Cohen’s κ κ kappa\kappa 的均值；以及 (iv) 模型与人工多数标签之间的 Cohen’s κ κ kappa\kappa 。仅当所有必需的标注者都提供了非空标签时，某条目才计入统计量。置信区间为 95 % 95 % 95%95 \% 百分位区间（第 2.5 个和第 97.5 个百分位） ，来自 2,000 次重抽样的无参数自助法。
To annotate these messages, we replicate the procedure from Section 3. For each conversation, the classifier is applied to a randomly selected user message along with up to the 10 preceding messages (each truncated to 5,000 characters). Because this context can be lengthy, human annotators also received a one-sentence précis of the preceding messages, generated using the following prompt:
为对这些消息进行标注，我们复制第 3 节中的程序。对于每个对话，分类器应用于随机选择的一条用户消息及最多前 10 条消息（每条截断为 5,000 字符）。由于该上下文可能较长，人工标注者还收到了对前述消息的一句概述，该概述使用以下提示生成：
-----
You are an internal tool that writes a one-sentence precis of a
message from a user to an AI chatbot, based on the context of the
previous messages before it. Write a precis of the user intent in the
last user message of this conversation, 25 words at most.
E.g. 'User is rewriting email to neighbors about
plumbing to be more friendly,'
or 'User is complaining about grandmother'
or 'User is asking for help fixing python databricks error.'

If the conversation changes topic just use the topic of
the final message from the user.
Always use English in your response. Always start
the precis with 'User is.'
Don't share anything about the user's name,
gender identity, location, email or phone number
or anything that could be personally identifiable.
For the Interaction Quality task, annotators additionally saw the next user message to evaluate any sentiment expressed by the user regarding their level of satisfaction. Because assistant messages tend to be very long, and can require a subject matter expert to evaluate accurately, human annotators were only provided with the final user message, not the assistant response. In-house annotators labeled each item, with ground truth defined as the plurality label 32 32 ^(32){ }^{32} when more than two annotators participated. A development set (46 items) was used for prompt and model selection; all results below are computed on a disjoint holdout set.
在“交互质量”任务中，标注员另外查看了下一条用户消息，以评估用户表达的关于其满意度的任何情绪。由于助手消息通常非常长，并且可能需要主题专家才能准确评估，人工标注员仅提供了最后一条用户消息，而非助手回复。内部标注员对每一项进行了标注，真值定义为在超过两名标注员参与时的多数标签 32 32 ^(32){ }^{32} 。使用了一个开发集（46 项）用于提示和模型选择；下面所有结果均在一个不相交的保留集上计算。
We use GPT-5-mini for all tasks except Interaction Quality, for which GPT-5 was selected based on development-set performance.
我们对除“交互质量”外的所有任务都使用 GPT-5-mini，基于开发集性能，GPT-5 被选用于“交互质量”任务。

B. 1 Results
B.1 结果

B.1.1 Work-Related Classifier
B.1.1 工作相关分类器

As shown in Table 5, model-plurality agreement is high (Cohen’s κ = 0.83 κ = 0.83 kappa=0.83\kappa=0.83 ), exceeding the mean human-human agreement ( κ = 0.66 κ = 0.66 kappa=0.66\kappa=0.66 ). The heatmap in Figure 25 indicates close alignment with the human plurality and limited systematic bias.
如表 5 所示，多模型多数意见一致性很高（Cohen’s κ = 0.83 κ = 0.83 kappa=0.83\kappa=0.83 ），高于人类之间的平均一致性（ κ = 0.66 κ = 0.66 kappa=0.66\kappa=0.66 ）。图 25 的热力图显示与人类多数意见高度一致且系统性偏差有限。

B.1.2 Asking/Doing/Expressing Classifier
B.1.2 Asking/Doing/Expressing 分类器

Human annotations exhibit substantial agreement (mean human-human Cohen’s κ = 0.60 κ = 0.60 kappa=0.60\kappa=0.60 ), and the classifier improves on this benchmark with κ = 0.74 κ = 0.74 kappa=0.74\kappa=0.74 against the human plurality (Table 5). Figures 26 and 27 show that most confusion arises between Asking and Doing; the classifier is somewhat more likely than humans to assign Doing. This pattern suggests that the prominence of Asking use cases in our main results is unlikely to be an artifact of misclassification.
人工标注表现出显著一致性（人类之间平均 Cohen’s κ = 0.60 κ = 0.60 kappa=0.60\kappa=0.60 ），且该分类器在与人类多数意见比较时以 κ = 0.74 κ = 0.74 kappa=0.74\kappa=0.74 提升了这一基准（表 5）。图 26 和图 27 显示大部分混淆发生在 Asking 与 Doing 之间；分类器比人类更倾向于判定为 Doing。该模式表明我们主要结果中 Asking 用例的突出位置不太可能是分类错误的产物。

B.1.3 Conversation Topic
B.1.3 会话主题

Agreement between the model and the human plurality is moderate to substantial (Cohen’s κ = 0.56 κ = 0.56 kappa=0.56\kappa=0.56 ), improving on the mean human-human agreement ( κ = 0.47 κ = 0.47 kappa=0.47\kappa=0.47 ). Misclassifications are concentrated between Seeking Information and Practical Guidance (Figure 28), which are conceptually adjacent categories. Relative to human annotators, the model under-labels Seeking Information, Technical Help, and Self-Expression, and over-labels Practical Guidance, Multimedia, and Other (Figure 29).
模型与多数人类的协议为中等到显著（Cohen’s κ = 0.56 κ = 0.56 kappa=0.56\kappa=0.56 ），优于人类之间的平均一致性（ κ = 0.47 κ = 0.47 kappa=0.47\kappa=0.47 ）。错误分类集中在“寻求信息”和“实用指导”之间（图 28），这两个类别在概念上相邻。与人工标注者相比，模型对“寻求信息”、“技术帮助”和“自我表达”标注不足，而对“实用指导”、“多媒体”和“其他”标注过多（图 29）。

B.1.4 O*NET Intermediate Work Activity
B.1.4 O*NET 中级工作活动

Two human labelers labeled 100 WildChat messages over 332 O*NET IWAs, with an additional category for when a message was ambiguous. Human labels were compared with LLM outputs. In practice, we found the ambiguous category was chosen when the user was simply greeting the model or submitted an empty prompt. In this validation set, we report Fleiss’s κ κ kappa\kappa for both the direct IWA classification ( κ = 0.47 κ = 0.47 kappa=0.47\kappa=0.47 ), as well as the GWA aggregation ( κ = 0.40 κ = 0.40 kappa=0.40\kappa=0.40 ). When only examining human outputs we see Cohen’s κ κ kappa\kappa of 0.27 . From review, we observe this moderate human-pair agreement due to the large number of potential classes (IWA has 332 activities) as well as inherent ambiguity in the messages. For instance, if a user in the WildChat dataset was trying to generate a fictional short story, one human label might be Develop news, entertainment, or artistic content, while another human label could be Write material for artistic or commercial purposes. These two IWAs also belong to different GWAs despite being conceptually similar.
两名人工标注者对来自 332 个 O*NET IWA 的 100 条 WildChat 消息进行了标注，并为消息含糊不清的情况增加了一个类别。人工标注结果与 LLM 输出进行了比较。实际上，我们发现当用户仅向模型打招呼或提交空提示时，会选择含糊类别。在该验证集中，我们报告了直接 IWA 分类（ κ = 0.47 κ = 0.47 kappa=0.47\kappa=0.47 ）以及 GWA 聚合（ κ = 0.40 κ = 0.40 kappa=0.40\kappa=0.40 ）的 Fleiss’s κ κ kappa\kappa 。仅检查人工输出时，我们看到 Cohen’s κ κ kappa\kappa 为 0.27。通过审查，我们观察到这种中等的人对人一致性是由于可能类别众多（IWA 有 332 个活动）以及消息本身固有的模糊性。例如，如果 WildChat 数据集中某用户试图生成一篇虚构短篇小说，一个人工标注可能是 Develop news, entertainment, or artistic content，而另一个人工标注可能是 Write material for artistic or commercial purposes。尽管这两个 IWA 在概念上相似，它们仍然属于不同的 GWA。

B.1.5 Interaction Quality Classifier

Human and model annotations of interaction quality are noisy. The classifier attains only slight agreement with the human plurality (Cohen’s κ = 0.14 κ = 0.14 kappa=0.14\kappa=0.14 ), below the likewise modest mean human-human agreement ( κ = 0.20 κ = 0.20 kappa=0.20\kappa=0.20; Table 5). Figures 30 and 31 show weak concordance overall and a mild tendency for the model to assign Bad less frequently than humans. This contrasts with our small development set, in which GPT-5 labeled Bad more often than humans. We retain this classifier because these κ κ kappa\kappa statistics primarily highlight the inherent difficulty of inferring the user’s latent satisfaction from text alone.
人与模型对交互质量的标注都有噪声。分类器仅与人类多数意见达成轻微一致（Cohen’s κ = 0.14 κ = 0.14 kappa=0.14\kappa=0.14 ），低于同样不高的人-人平均一致度（ κ = 0.20 κ = 0.20 kappa=0.20\kappa=0.20 ；表 5）。图 30 和图 31 显示总体一致性较弱，且模型比人类略少标注为 Bad。这与我们的小型开发集形成对比，在该开发集中 GPT-5 比人类更频繁地标注 Bad。我们保留该分类器，因为这些 κ κ kappa\kappa 统计数据主要突出了仅凭文本推断用户潜在满意度的固有困难。
While this latent “prior” is unobserved in our validation data, it is partially observable when users provide explicit thumbs-up/down feedback. To assess whether the classifier captures a signal aligned
虽然在我们的验证数据中无法观测到这种潜在“先验”，但当用户提供明确的点赞/点踩反馈时，它是部分可观测的。为评估分类器是否捕捉到与之对齐的信号
Figure 31: Figure 30: Agreement Between Model and Plurality for Interaction Quality
图 31：图 30：模型与多数意见在交互质量上的一致性
Figure 32: Figure 31: Bias Between Model and Plurality for Interaction Quality
图 32：图 31：模型与多数意见在交互质量上的偏差
with user experience, we link model predictions to voluntary feedback on assistant messages. We draw a 1 -in-10,000 sample of conversations from June 2024 to June 2025 and retain cases where (i) the assistant message received explicit feedback and (ii) the user sent a subsequent message that our classifier can score, yielding roughly 60,000 eligible items. This is a restricted sample that may not be fully representative of all interactions, but it offers a unique lens on the classifier’s ability to proxy user satisfaction.
在用户体验方面，我们将模型预测与对助手消息的自愿反馈联系起来。我们从 2024 年 6 月至 2025 年 6 月抽取了 1/10,000 的对话样本，并保留以下情况：(i) 助手消息收到了明确反馈，且 (ii) 用户发送了后续消息且我们的分类器可以对其打分，最终获得大约 60,000 条符合条件的样本。该样本受限，可能不能完全代表所有交互，但它为评估分类器替代用户满意度的能力提供了独特视角。
Figure 32 shows that Unknown classifications are split roughly evenly between thumbs-down and thumbs-up feedback. Thumbs-up comprises 86 % 86 % 86%86 \% of all feedback. Conversations with thumbs-down feedback are about equally likely to be classified as Good or Bad, whereas thumbs-up feedback is 9.5 times more likely to be followed by a message classified as Good.
图 32 显示，“未知”分类在点赞与点踩之间大致均分。点赞占所有反馈的 86 % 86 % 86%86 \% 。收到点踩反馈的对话被分类为“好”或“差”的概率大致相当，而收到点赞反馈后出现被分类为“好”的后续消息的概率是点踩后的 9.5 倍。

Table 6: Figure 35: Commonly requested GWAs among all queries (work-related and non-work-related, combined), ranked by frequency within broad occupation groups (two-digit SOC codes). (IE: 1 represents the most frequently requested GWA for that occupation). X's indicate that the ranking is unavailable since fewer than 100 users from that occupation group requested that specific GWA. Two occupation groups are omitted because no GWA was requested by more than 100 users from a single occupation group. These omitted occupation groups (with corresponding SOC2 codes) are "Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance" (37) and "Farming, Fishing, and Forestry" (45).
表 6：图 35：在所有查询中（工作相关与非工作相关合并）常被请求的 GWA，按广泛职业组（两位 SOC 代码）内的频率排序。（即：1 表示该职业中被请求频率最高的 GWA）。当某职业组中请求该特定 GWA 的用户少于 100 人时，用“X”表示排名不可用。有两个职业组被省略，因为没有任何单一职业组中有超过 100 名用户请求某个 GWA。被省略的职业组及其对应的 SOC2 代码为“建筑物和场地清洁与维护”（37）和“农业、渔业与林业”（45）。

  2. 7 7 ^(7){ }^{7} The difference between Practical Guidance and Seeking Information is that the former is highly customized to the user and can be adapted based on conversation and follow-up, whereas the latter is factual information that should be the same for all users. For example, users interested in running might ask ChatGPT for the Boston Marathon qualifying times by age and gender (Seeking Information), or they might ask for a customized workout plan that matches their goals and current level of fitness (Practical Guidance).
    7 7 ^(7){ }^{7} Practical Guidance 与 Seeking Information 的区别在于，前者是高度针对用户的，并且可以根据对话和后续跟进进行调整，而后者是应对所有用户都相同的事实性信息。例如，想跑步的用户可能会向 ChatGPT 询问按年龄和性别划分的波士顿马拉松合格时间（Seeking Information），或者他们可能会请求一份根据其目标和当前体能水平定制的训练计划（Practical Guidance）。

We believe the discrepancy is partly due to the difference in types of users between Claude and ChatGPT, additionally Handa et al. (2025) only includes queries that “possibly involve an occupational task”.
    8 8 ^(8){ }^{8} Handa 等人（2025）报告称 37 % 37 % 37%37 \% 的对话被归入“计算机与数学”职业类别，他们的图 12 显示 30 % 30 % 30%30 \% 或更多的所有推断任务为编程或与 IT 相关。我们认为这种差异部分是由于 Claude 与 ChatGPT 之间用户类型的差异所致，此外 Handa 等人（2025）仅包括“可能涉及职业任务”的查询。

For logged-out users, the count is based on distinct browser cookies; this would double-count people if someone returns to ChatGPT after clearing their cookies, or if they access ChatGPT with two different devices in the same week.
    20 20 ^(20){ }^{20} 请注意，当一个人拥有两个账户时（或对于未登录用户，一个人在两个设备上使用），我们对不同账户的计数预计会略多于不同人的计数。对于已登录用户，计数基于不同的登录凭证（电子邮件地址），一个人可能拥有多个账户。对于未登录用户，计数基于不同的浏览器 cookie；如果用户清除了 cookie 后再次访问 ChatGPT，或在同一周使用两个不同设备访问 ChatGPT，则会导致重复计数。
